    76	def derive_valuation(payload, fx):
    77	    """`{ev_usd_m, ev_sales, ev_ebitda, reporting_ccy, reason}` for one row.
    78	
    79	    ⛑ THE VENDOR'S `enterpriseValue` IS NOT IN ANY CURRENCY, so it is never
    80	    published. Measured 2026-09-08 across the live payloads: Yahoo's EV is
    81	    `marketCap` (in the QUOTE currency) plus `totalDebt - totalCash` (in the
    82	    REPORTING currency), summed as if they shared a unit --
    83	    `(EV - marketCap) / (totalDebt - totalCash)` is 1.000 for TAK, 1.004 for NVO,
    84	    0.990 for LLY, 1.053 for CYH. For a US row the two currencies are the same and
    85	    the sum is harmless; for an ADR it is a number in no unit at all.
    86	
    87	    ⛑ THAT IS WHY TAGGING EV WITH `financialCurrency` AND CONVERTING IS WRONG,
    88	    and it was the first fix proposed. It produces Takeda at USD 33.3bn against a
    89	    true ~USD 91.8bn: a PLAUSIBLE wrong number, which is worse than the absurd
    90	    USD 5.1tn it replaces, because absurd numbers get noticed and plausible ones
    91	    get used.
    92	
    93	    So: trust only primitives that each carry ONE known currency, and compute.
    94	
    95	        EV      = marketCap x fx(quote)  +  (totalDebt - totalCash) x fx(reporting)
    96	        EV/S    = EV / (totalRevenue x fx(reporting))
    97	        EV/EBITDA = EV / (ebitda x fx(reporting))
    98	
    99	    This also repairs a class that has nothing to do with currency: ASML and
   100	    argenx have entirely sane components and only the vendor's DERIVED EV is
   101	    broken (argenx quote and reporting are both USD and its EV was still 25x its
   102	    market cap). Computed: TAK EV 5,134,819 -> 91,798; NVO EV/S 0.9 -> 4.3;
   103	    ASML 1035.7 -> 15.9; ARGX 302.9 -> 11.1; CYH unchanged at 0.9, correctly.
   104	
   105	    ⛑ NO FALLBACK TO THE VENDOR EV WHEN A COMPONENT IS MISSING. That would
   106	    reintroduce exactly the undetectable garbage class, and it cannot be screened
   107	    out afterwards: Novo's published EV is 37% high while sitting INSIDE any
   108	    sane EV/market-cap band, and CYH is correct while sitting outside it. A ratio
   109	    test flags the innocent and passes the guilty, so the only honest gate is
   110	    "are this field's own inputs present and convertible" -- `reason` says which
   111	    one was not.
   112	
   113	    Known limit, stated because the number should not imply more precision than
   114	    it has: component EV omits minority interest and preferred stock, so it reads
   115	    ~0.5% below Yahoo's own primary-listing EV for TAK and ~2% for NVO. That is
   116	    far inside the error of any spot-FX conversion.
   117	    """
   118	    out = {"ev_usd_m": None, "ev_sales": None, "ev_ebitda": None,
   119	           "net_debt_usd": None, "revenue_usd_m": None,
   120	           "reporting_ccy": None, "reason": None}
   121	
   122	    quote = (payload.get("currency") or "").strip()
   123	    report = (payload.get("financialCurrency") or "").strip()
   124	    out["reporting_ccy"] = report or None
   125	
   126	    mc = num(payload.get("marketCap"))
   127	    debt = num(payload.get("totalDebt"))
   128	    cash = num(payload.get("totalCash"))
   129	
   130	    # ── REVENUE IS GATED ON ITS OWN INPUTS, BEFORE ANY EV GATE ────────────────
   131	    # ⛑ Codex Medium #6, 2026-09-08. Revenue needs exactly three things: the
   132	    # figure, the reporting currency, and a usable rate for it. It does NOT need
   133	    # a market cap, a quote currency, debt or cash -- yet every one of those
   134	    # early-returned above it, and `reporting/generate.py` blanks `Revenue (TTM)`
   135	    # whenever `ev_usd_m` is None. Trigger: `totalRevenue = 5e9`, reporting USD,
   136	    # `marketCap = None` -> the commercial-biopharma classifier correctly sees
   137	    # $5bn while the performance report published Revenue TTM as blank.
   138	    #
   139	    # This is the function's own stated rule finally applied to this field: "are
   140	    # THIS field's own inputs present and convertible". `_revenue_usd_m` in
   141	    # `universe/commercial_biopharma.py` exists solely because revenue could not
   142	    # be trusted to come out of here; the two now agree by construction.
   143	    #
   144	    # Zero stays a real, publishable answer (a pre-revenue biotech); a negative
   145	    # is not a revenue figure and stays absent.
   146	    _rev = num(payload.get("totalRevenue"))
   147	    if report and _rev is not None and _rev >= 0:
   148	        _r_rate_only = fx.get(major_unit(report))
   149	        if _usable_rate(_r_rate_only):
   150	            _rev_usd_m = _rev * _r_rate_only / 1e6
   151	            if math.isfinite(_rev_usd_m):
   152	                out["revenue_usd_m"] = _rev_usd_m
   153	
   154	    if mc is None or mc <= 0:
   155	        # ⛑ `mc == 0` is NOT a small company, it is a vendor blank wearing a
   156	        # number (Codex, 2026-09-08). It sails past an `is None` check and makes
   157	        # EV collapse to net debt alone: Takeda came out at USD 33,003M -- which
   158	        # is, to the dollar, the same plausible-wrong figure the rejected
   159	        # financialCurrency fix produced. A wrong EV that looks reasonable is the
   160	        # one failure mode this whole function exists to prevent.
   161	        out["reason"] = "no marketCap"; return out
   162	    if not quote:
   163	        out["reason"] = "no quote currency"; return out
   164	    if not report:
   165	        # Absent for some rows in `.info`. That is a blank, never a fallback to
   166	        # the quote currency -- assuming they match is the original defect.
   167	        out["reason"] = "no financialCurrency"; return out
   168	    if debt is None or cash is None:
   169	        out["reason"] = "no totalDebt/totalCash"; return out
   170	
   171	    # ⛑ A RATE MUST BE POSITIVE AND FINITE, not merely present (Codex,
   172	    # 2026-09-08). `fetch_aggregate_fx` can hand back 0.0 or a negative for a
   173	    # dead pair, and all three of those failed differently and badly:
   174	    #   0.0 on the reporting leg -> ZeroDivisionError in the EV/Sales
   175	    #     denominator. A CRASH, and it beat the `dead_fx` guard to the punch --
   176	    #     that guard runs AFTER this loop, so it could never report the thing it
   177	    #     exists to report. Ordering made a guard unreachable.
   178	    #   negative on the reporting leg -> a confident USD 25,470M for Takeda with
   179	    #     `reason: None`, i.e. published as though proven.
   180	    #   0.0 on the quote leg -> a near-zero EV, also with no reason.
   181	    # `is None` was the wrong test. "Can I actually convert with this?" is the
   182	    # right one, and it is asked of both legs before either is used.
   183	    q_rate = fx.get(major_unit(quote))
   184	    r_rate = fx.get(major_unit(report))
   185	    if not _usable_rate(q_rate):
   186	        out["reason"] = "no FX for %s" % quote; return out
   187	    if not _usable_rate(r_rate):
   188	        out["reason"] = "no FX for %s" % report; return out
   189	
   190	    # ⛑ `net_debt_usd` IS RETURNED, NOT RECOMPUTED BY THE CALLER (Fable, Low #4,
   191	    # 2026-09-08). `reporting/generate.py` used to re-derive this leg from the raw
   192	    # payload -- a SECOND implementation of a value this function had already
   193	    # proven, and it skipped `num()`, so a vendor string `"5.4e12"` passed the
   194	    # checks here and then raised TypeError on `debt - cash` in the caller,
   195	    # aborting the whole report. One computation, one place.
   196	    net_debt_usd = (debt - cash) * r_rate
   197	    ev_usd = mc * q_rate + net_debt_usd
   198	    if not math.isfinite(ev_usd):
   199	        out["reason"] = "non-finite EV"; return out
   200	    out["ev_usd_m"] = ev_usd / 1e6
   201	    out["net_debt_usd"] = net_debt_usd if math.isfinite(net_debt_usd) else None
   202	
   203	    # Belt and braces on the denominator itself. `r_rate` is positive and both
   204	    # figures are checked positive above, so the product should be too -- but a
   205	    # tiny revenue times a tiny rate can underflow to exactly 0.0, and this is a
   206	    # division. Guarding the RESULT (as positive_multiple does) is too late; the
   207	    # exception is raised before it ever sees a value.
   208	    # ⛑ REVENUE IS RETURNED, NOT LEFT AS AN INTERMEDIATE. It is already computed
   209	    # here (`totalRevenue x fx(reporting)`) and it is the input to the commercial
   210	    # -biopharma classification and to the revenue-vs-market-cap screen. The
   211	    # alternative every consumer reached for first was deriving it as
   212	    # `EV / (EV/Sales)`, which inherits any error in EITHER input and returns
   213	    # nothing for the rows with no EV/Sales at all.
   214	    #
   215	    # Note ZERO is a real, publishable answer -- a pre-revenue biotech -- and is
   216	    # kept distinct from None. `ev_sales` still requires a POSITIVE denominator,
   217	    # so a zero-revenue row reports revenue 0.0 and no multiple.
   218	    # `revenue_usd_m` was already set above, on its own inputs alone. Only the
   219	    # MULTIPLE is computed here, because that one genuinely needs the EV.
   220	    rev = num(payload.get("totalRevenue"))
   221	    if rev is not None and rev > 0 and rev * r_rate > 0:
   222	        out["ev_sales"] = positive_multiple(ev_usd / (rev * r_rate))
   223	    ebitda = num(payload.get("ebitda"))
   224	    if ebitda is not None and ebitda > 0 and ebitda * r_rate > 0:
   225	        out["ev_ebitda"] = positive_multiple(ev_usd / (ebitda * r_rate))
   226	    return out

    65	def _blank_ev_fields(fund):
    66	    """Blank every field derived from the vendor's EV. Never a fallback.
    67	
    68	    ⛑ THE GATE IS MISSING-PROOF, NOT RATIO-ANOMALY. Novo's vendor EV was 37%
    69	    high while sitting INSIDE any sane EV/market-cap band; CYH is correct while
    70	    sitting well outside one. A ratio screen flags the innocent and passes the
    71	    guilty, so the only honest question is "are this field's own inputs present
    72	    and convertible". Blank the FIELDS, never the row -- Mkt Cap, Price and the
    73	    returns are proven independently of EV.
    74	
    75	    ⛑ `Revenue (TTM)` IS IN THE LIST BUT IS RESTORED BY THE CALLER when its own
    76	    inputs hold (Codex Medium #6, 2026-09-08). It stays in `EV_DERIVED_FIELDS`
    77	    because the no-primitives path genuinely cannot prove it either, so blanking
    78	    remains the correct DEFAULT; what was wrong was treating a missing market cap
    79	    or debt figure as evidence about revenue. Revenue needs the figure, the
    80	    reporting currency and its rate -- nothing else -- and `derive_valuation` now
    81	    computes it before any EV gate.
    82	    """
    83	    for f in EV_DERIVED_FIELDS:
    84	        fund[f] = None

    87	def _recompute_ev_from_primitives(all_fundamentals, all_currencies, fx, skip=()):
    88	    """Replace EV / Net Debt / EV-multiples with values computed from primitives.
    89	
    90	    Returns (computed, blanked). `skip` is the set of tickers the caller already
    91	    blanked for having no usable quote rate.
    92	
    93	    ⛑ `skip` IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. Found by this module's own test: a row whose
    94	    `Mkt Cap` had just been blanked for a dead rate got its EV recomputed anyway,
    95	    because `derive_valuation` reads the quote currency off the row's OWN
    96	    `_valuation` payload while the blanking decision was made from
    97	    `all_currencies`. Two sources of truth for one fact, and the row published an
    98	    ENTERPRISE VALUE WITH NO MARKET CAP -- internally impossible, and the kind of
    99	    thing a reader trusts because the number itself looks fine.
   100	
   101	    ⛑ WHY THIS OVERWRITES RATHER THAN FILLS A GAP. `yfinance_provider` still
   102	    populates `Enterprise Value` and `Net Debt` from the vendor, because
   103	    `provider_chain._is_success` counts EV as a quality field and `_merge_partial`
   104	    fills any None from the NEXT provider -- so leaving them empty upstream would
   105	    have pulled FMP's identically mixed-unit EV in behind it and reintroduced the
   106	    defect through the fallback. Making one site the authority is what closes
   107	    that door; a row with no primitives is blanked here rather than trusted.
   108	    """
   109	    computed, blanked = 0, 0
   110	    skip = set(skip)
   111	    for yf_t, fund in all_fundamentals.items():
   112	        if yf_t in skip:
   113	            continue          # already blanked; its market cap is unpublishable
   114	        prim = fund.get("_valuation")
   115	        if not isinstance(prim, dict):
   116	            # No primitives: an FMP/AlphaVantage row, or a cache entry predating
   117	            # them. We cannot show that its EV is in any single currency, so we
   118	            # do not publish it. Absent is a true statement; a mixed unit is not.
   119	            _blank_ev_fields(fund)
   120	            blanked += 1
   121	            continue
   122	        val = derive_valuation(prim, fx)
   123	        if val["ev_usd_m"] is None:
   124	            _blank_ev_fields(fund)
   125	            # ⛑ ...but revenue is not an EV field (Codex Medium #6, 2026-09-08).
   126	            # A row with $5bn of revenue, a reporting currency and a live rate
   127	            # has PROVEN its revenue, whatever is missing from the EV side. It
   128	            # was published blank because a market cap was absent -- while the
   129	            # commercial-biopharma classifier, reading the same primitives,
   130	            # correctly saw the $5bn. Two surfaces, one cache, opposite answers.
   131	            if val["revenue_usd_m"] is not None:
   132	                fund["Revenue (TTM)"] = val["revenue_usd_m"] * 1e6
   133	            blanked += 1
   134	            continue
   135	        ev_usd = val["ev_usd_m"] * 1e6
   136	        fund["Enterprise Value"] = ev_usd
   137	        # Net debt is the reporting-currency leg, converted on the REPORTING
   138	        # rate -- the whole point. It comes back FROM `derive_valuation` rather
   139	        # than being re-derived here: re-deriving was a second implementation of
   140	        # a leg already proven, and it skipped `num()`, so a vendor string
   141	        # `"5.4e12"` raised TypeError and aborted the run (Fable, 2026-09-08).
   142	        fund["Net Debt"] = val["net_debt_usd"]
   143	        fund["EV/S"] = val["ev_sales"]
   144	        fund["EV/EBITDA"] = val["ev_ebitda"]
   145	        # ⛑ Revenue in USD, from the primitive rather than derived as
   146	        # `EV / (EV/Sales)`. The derived form inherits any error in EITHER input
   147	        # and returns nothing at all for a row with no EV/Sales -- which is every
   148	        # pre-revenue biotech, i.e. exactly the population a commercial-stage
   149	        # classification has to separate. ZERO is a real answer here and is kept
   150	        # distinct from None.
   151	        fund["Revenue (TTM)"] = (val["revenue_usd_m"] * 1e6
   152	                                 if val["revenue_usd_m"] is not None else None)
   153	        computed += 1
   154	
   155	    # ⛑ `_valuation` IS TRANSPORT, AND IT MUST NOT REACH THE ROW. `calcs.
   156	    # build_result_row` does `row.update(fund)`, so every key here becomes a
   157	    # DataFrame column -- and this one holds a dict, which openpyxl cannot write.
   158	    # That is the shape of a crash AFTER the report is half-built, the same way
   159	    # an `inf` market cap once killed the coverage build after it had already
   160	    # installed the workbook. Consumed here, dropped here, for every row
   161	    # including the skipped and blanked ones.
   162	    for fund in all_fundamentals.values():
   163	        fund.pop("_valuation", None)
   164	    return computed, blanked
   165	
   166	
   167	def _convert_aggregates_to_usd(all_fundamentals, all_currencies, fx=None):
   168	    """Convert company AGGREGATES to USD in place. Returns (converted, blanked).
   169	
   170	    ⛑ AGGREGATES USE THE MAJOR UNIT (2026-09-08). This used
   171	    `fetch_fx_rates(currency)` on the raw quote code, and Yahoo answers a minor
   172	    code with a rate that is right for the PRICE and wrong for the AGGREGATES:
   173	    `ZAcUSD=X` returns the CENTS rate (0.000625 in the live cache), so a
   174	    Johannesburg market cap -- which Yahoo reports in whole rand -- was converted
   175	    at 1/100. **Aspen Pharmacare's R65.6bn published as USD 43M in this report**,
   176	    the same defect fixed in the coverage books on 2026-09-07 and not carried
   177	    across to this lane. `fetch_aggregate_fx` requests the major unit and returns
   178	    it under both keys, so looking up the raw quote currency cannot return the
   179	    minor rate.
   180	
   181	    ⛑ ONLY AN EXPLICIT "USD" BYPASSES CONVERSION (Codex, High). This read
   182	    `all_currencies.get(yf_t, "USD")` and skipped on a falsy value, so a MISSING
   183	    or EMPTY currency took the same path as a genuine US row and published the
   184	    raw aggregate under a USD heading. That state is reachable --
   185	    `provider_chain._is_success` documents currency as required and never checks
   186	    it -- so a Japanese payload with `Mkt Cap = 4e12` and `currency = ""` would
   187	    read as USD 4,000B and skew every cap-weighted basket built from it.
   188	
   189	    ⛑ AN UNUSABLE RATE BLANKS THE FIELD. This was `continue`, which left a
   190	    local-currency figure under a column headed USD -- a number that reads as
   191	    converted and is not. Absent is a true statement; a wrong unit is not.
   192	
   193	    `fx` is injectable for tests only; production passes None and fetches.
   194	    """
   195	    if fx is None:
   196	        # ⛑ THE UNION OF BOTH CURRENCY SETS, not just the quote currencies.
   197	        # `all_currencies` holds what each row QUOTES in. EV and Net Debt also
   198	        # need the rate for what it REPORTS in, and for an ADR those differ by
   199	        # definition -- Takeda quotes USD and reports JPY. Requesting only the
   200	        # quote set left `fx` with no JPY, so `derive_valuation` could not prove
   201	        # the reporting leg and BLANKED EV for the whole ADR book.
   202	        #
   203	        # It failed safe rather than publishing a wrong number, which is the
   204	        # design working -- but silently blanking every ADR's EV is still a
   205	        # functional outage, and it only looked fine in testing because the
   206	        # verification passed `fx` in explicitly and so never exercised this
   207	        # branch. Same trap as `test_the_production_path_fetches_AGGREGATE_rates`
   208	        # in tests/test_fx_minor_units.py, which exists for exactly this reason.
   209	        #
   210	        # It would ALSO have partly worked by luck: JPY and EUR are quoted by
   211	        # other rows in the universe, so those ADRs would resolve while a
   212	        # reporting currency no row happens to quote would not. Correct by
   213	        # caller coincidence is not correct.
   214	        wanted = {c for c in all_currencies.values() if c and c != "USD"}
   215	        wanted |= {(f.get("_valuation") or {}).get("financialCurrency")
   216	                   for f in all_fundamentals.values()}
   217	        wanted = {c for c in wanted if c and c != "USD"}
   218	        fx = fetch_aggregate_fx(wanted) if wanted else {"USD": 1.0}
   219	
   220	    converted, unconvertible = 0, []
   221	    for yf_t, fund in all_fundamentals.items():
   222	        currency = all_currencies.get(yf_t)
   223	        if currency == "USD":
   224	            continue
   225	        # ⛑ LOOK UP THE MAJOR UNIT, not the raw quote code. `fetch_aggregate_fx`
   226	        # already aliases the major rate under the minor key, so this is
   227	        # belt-and-braces -- but without it the correctness of this function
   228	        # depends on WHICH dict the caller handed it, which is caller convention
   229	        # rather than a property. A test that passes a plain
   230	        # `{"ZAc": <cents rate>}` proves the difference: it converted Aspen at
   231	        # 1/100 until this line read `major_unit(currency)`.
   232	        # ⛑ `_usable_rate`, NOT `is None` (Fable, Medium, 2026-09-08). Codex
   233	        # round 3 fixed this class inside `derive_valuation` and it stayed live
   234	        # in this loop, which converts `Mkt Cap`. `fetch_fx_rates` does a bare
   235	        # `float(hist["Close"].iloc[-1])` with no finiteness check and caches the
   236	        # result for 12h, so 0.0 and NaN are both reachable: a 0.0 rate published
   237	        # `Mkt Cap = 0.0` under a USD heading, and NaN put a NaN into the
   238	        # DataFrame and on into openpyxl. A rate must be usable, not merely present.
   239	        rate = fx.get(major_unit(currency)) if currency else None
   240	        if not _usable_rate(rate):
   241	            for field in USD_AGGREGATE_FIELDS:
   242	                if fund.get(field) is not None:
   243	                    fund[field] = None
   244	            _blank_ev_fields(fund)
   245	            unconvertible.append((yf_t, currency or "<no currency>"))
   246	            continue
   247	        for field in USD_AGGREGATE_FIELDS:
   248	            val = fund.get(field)
   249	            if val is not None:
   250	                fund[field] = val * rate
   251	        converted += 1
   252	
   253	    # ⛑ EV AND NET DEBT ARE RECOMPUTED, NOT CONVERTED -- for EVERY row, USD ones
   254	    # included. The loop above is correct for `Mkt Cap` and only for `Mkt Cap`:
   255	    # it applies ONE rate to three fields, and two of them are not in that
   256	    # currency. See `providers/valuation.derive_valuation` for the measurement.
   257	    # A US row is included because the vendor's EV is broken there too for a
   258	    # separate reason -- argenx quotes AND reports USD and its EV was 25x its
   259	    # market cap -- so "same currency" is not the same claim as "correct".
   260	    ev_ok, ev_blanked = _recompute_ev_from_primitives(
   261	        all_fundamentals, all_currencies, fx, skip={t for t, _ in unconvertible})
   262	
   263	    if converted:
   264	        logger.info("Converted Mkt Cap/EV/Net Debt to USD for %d non-USD tickers",
   265	                    converted)
   266	    if unconvertible:
   267	        logger.warning(
   268	            "No usable currency/FX rate for %d ticker(s); Mkt Cap/EV/Net Debt "
   269	            "BLANKED rather than published unconverted: %s",
   270	            len(unconvertible),
   271	            ", ".join("%s(%s)" % (t, c) for t, c in sorted(unconvertible)[:15]))
   272	    logger.info("EV/Net Debt computed from primitives for %d ticker(s)", ev_ok)
   273	    if ev_blanked:
   274	        logger.warning(
   275	            "EV/Net Debt/EV-multiples BLANKED for %d ticker(s) whose inputs "
   276	            "could not be proven (no fallback to the vendor's mixed-unit EV)",
   277	            ev_blanked)
   278	    return converted, len(unconvertible)
   279	
   280	def _load_phase1_tickers():
   281	    """Read all five-state position tickers from exports.
   282	
   283	    Phase 1 of the historical-valuation feature enriches every name with a
   284	    personal trading-state relationship: Portfolio, Researching, Following
   285	    for Interest, Ready to Buy, Ready to Short. Following-for-Interest names
   286	    are included because earnings-season context benefits from the same
   287	    historical-valuation columns the other states rely on.
   288	
   289	    Returns an empty set if the export files are missing — the caller treats
   290	    that as "skip enrichment" and leaves the columns blank.
   291	    """
   292	    from pathlib import Path
   293	    exports_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "exports"
   294	    tickers = set()
   295	    for fname in (
   296	        "portfolio.json",
   297	        "researching.json",
   298	        "following_for_interest.json",
   299	        "ready_to_buy.json",
   300	        "ready_to_short.json",
   300	        "ready_to_short.json",
   301	    ):
   302	        path = exports_dir / fname
   303	        if not path.exists():
   304	            continue
   305	        try:
   306	            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   307	            tickers.update(data.keys())
   308	        except Exception as e:
   309	            logger.warning("Failed to read %s for history universe: %s", fname, e)
   310	    return tickers

   313	def _hist_columns_from_payload(payload):
   314	    """Convert a fetch_history result dict into the history columns.
   315	
   316	    Returns a dict with keys matching `HIST_COLS` (5Y block, 10Y block, and the
   317	    `History Status` marker). Any field that can't be computed (insufficient
   318	    data) is set to None — the Excel writer renders those as N/A. Nothing is
   319	    ever defaulted to 0: a 0 in a P/E-min column would silently corrupt every
   320	    downstream valuation screen.
   321	
   322	    The 5Y and 10Y windows are two slices of the SAME annual series, so the 10Y
   323	    columns add no API cost.
   324	    """
   325	    pe_ttm = payload.get("pe_ttm")
   326	    pe_history = payload.get("pe_history") or []
   327	    evs_history = payload.get("evs_history") or []
   328	
   329	    pe_5 = stats_from_series(pe_history[:5], current=pe_ttm)
   330	    pe_10 = stats_from_series(pe_history[:10], current=pe_ttm)
   331	    # For EV/S vs-avg the "current" comparison uses the existing EV/S (TTM)
   332	    # column populated by the provider chain, which isn't in scope here — pass
   333	    # current=None and let the row-injection step below fill vs_avg_pct.
   334	    evs_5 = stats_from_series(evs_history[:5], current=None)
   335	    evs_10 = stats_from_series(evs_history[:10], current=None)
   336	
   337	    return {
   338	        "P/E (TTM)": pe_ttm,
   339	        "P/E 5Y Avg": pe_5["avg"],
   340	        "P/E 5Y +1σ": pe_5["plus_1sd"],
   341	        "P/E 5Y -1σ": pe_5["minus_1sd"],
   342	        "P/E 5Y Min": pe_5["min"],
   343	        "P/E 5Y Max": pe_5["max"],
   344	        "P/E vs 5Y Avg": pe_5["vs_avg_pct"],
   345	        "EV/S 5Y Avg": evs_5["avg"],
   346	        "EV/S 5Y +1σ": evs_5["plus_1sd"],
   347	        "EV/S 5Y -1σ": evs_5["minus_1sd"],
   348	        "EV/S 5Y Min": evs_5["min"],
   349	        "EV/S 5Y Max": evs_5["max"],
   350	        "EV/S vs 5Y Avg": None,  # filled later once TTM EV/S is in scope
   351	        "P/E 10Y Avg": pe_10["avg"],
   352	        "P/E 10Y +1σ": pe_10["plus_1sd"],
   353	        "P/E 10Y -1σ": pe_10["minus_1sd"],
   354	        "P/E 10Y Min": pe_10["min"],
   355	        "P/E 10Y Max": pe_10["max"],
   356	        "P/E vs 10Y Avg": pe_10["vs_avg_pct"],
   357	        "EV/S 10Y Avg": evs_10["avg"],
   358	        "EV/S 10Y +1σ": evs_10["plus_1sd"],
   359	        "EV/S 10Y -1σ": evs_10["minus_1sd"],
   360	        "EV/S 10Y Min": evs_10["min"],
   361	        "EV/S 10Y Max": evs_10["max"],
   362	        "EV/S vs 10Y Avg": None,  # filled later once TTM EV/S is in scope
   363	        HIST_STATUS_COL: payload.get("status") or STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED,
   364	    }
   365	
   366	
   367	def _evs_vs_avg_pct(current_evs, evs_history, years=5):
   368	    """Compute (current TTM EV/S - N-year avg) / N-year avg * 100. None-safe."""
   369	    stats = stats_from_series((evs_history or [])[:years], current=current_evs)
   370	    return stats["vs_avg_pct"]

   373	def classify_sector_group(row):
   374	    """Classify a coverage row into a sector group based on Sector (JP) / Subsector (JP)."""
   375	    sector = str(row.get("Sector (JP)", "")).strip()
   376	    subsector = str(row.get("Subsector (JP)", "")).strip()
   377	    if sector in BIOPHARMA_VALUES or subsector in BIOPHARMA_VALUES:
   378	        return "Biopharma"
   379	    if sector in HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES or subsector in HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES:
   380	        return "HC Svcs & MedTech"
   381	    return "Following: Non-HC"

   384	def _split_into_segments(result_df):
   385	    """Split result_df into segment DataFrames keyed by tab name."""
   386	    segments = {"Consolidated": result_df}
   387	    sector = result_df.get("Sector (JP)", pd.Series(dtype="object")).fillna("").astype(str).str.strip()
   388	    subsector = result_df.get("Subsector (JP)", pd.Series(dtype="object")).fillna("").astype(str).str.strip()
   389	    biopharma_mask = sector.isin(BIOPHARMA_VALUES) | subsector.isin(BIOPHARMA_VALUES)
   390	    hc_svcs_mask = sector.isin(HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES) | subsector.isin(HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES)
   391	    non_hc_mask = ~biopharma_mask & ~hc_svcs_mask
   392	    segments["Biopharma"] = result_df[biopharma_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   393	    segments["HC Svcs & MedTech"] = result_df[hc_svcs_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   394	    segments["Following: Non-HC"] = result_df[non_hc_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   395	    return segments

   398	def _prepare_universe_rows(df, sample_mode=False, sample_set=None):
   399	    """Normalize and deduplicate the coverage universe once per run."""
   400	    working = df.copy()
   401	    working["Ticker"] = working["Ticker"].fillna("").astype(str).str.strip()
   402	    valid_mask = (working["Ticker"] != "") & (working["Ticker"] != "#N/A")
   403	    if sample_mode and sample_set is not None:
   404	        valid_mask &= working["Ticker"].str.upper().isin(sample_set)
   405	    working = working.loc[valid_mask].drop_duplicates(subset=["Ticker"], keep="first").reset_index(drop=True)
   406	
   407	    yf_tickers = []
   408	    for row in working[["Ticker", "Company Name", "Exchange"]].fillna("").to_dict("records"):
   409	        yf_tickers.append(
   410	            normalize_ticker(
   411	                str(row.get("Ticker", "")).strip(),
   412	                str(row.get("Company Name", "")).strip(),
   413	                str(row.get("Exchange", "")).strip(),
   414	            )
   415	        )
   416	    working["_yf_ticker"] = yf_tickers
   417	    return working

   420	def _build_additions_summary(additions_path):
   421	    """Parse the weekly additions markdown and return a plain-text summary.
   422	
   423	    Extracts the recommendations table and company summaries section to
   424	    include in the performance email body.
   425	    """
   426	    text = additions_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   427	    lines = []
   428	    lines.append("=== Weekly Coverage Universe Additions ===\n")
   429	
   430	    # Extract each row from the recommendations table (lines starting with | N |)
   431	    for m in re.finditer(
   432	        r"^\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|([^|]+)\|",
   433	        text, re.MULTILINE,
   434	    ):
   435	        num = m.group(1).strip()
   436	        company = m.group(2).strip().strip("*")
   437	        ticker = m.group(3).strip()
   438	        trigger = m.group(9).strip()
   439	        reason = m.group(11).strip()
   440	        lines.append(f"{num}. {ticker} ({company}) — {trigger} — {reason}")
   441	
   442	    # Extract company summaries
   443	    summary_match = re.search(
   444	        r"## Company Summaries\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n---|\n## |\Z)", text, re.DOTALL
   445	    )
   446	    if summary_match:
   447	        lines.append("\n--- Company Summaries ---\n")
   448	        lines.append(summary_match.group(1).strip())
   449	
   450	    return "\n".join(lines)
   451

   455	def _fmt_duration(seconds):
   456	    """Format seconds as human-readable duration."""
   457	    if seconds < 60:
   458	        return f"{seconds:.1f}s"
   459	    m, s = divmod(int(seconds), 60)
   460	    if m < 60:
   461	        return f"{m}m {s}s"
   462	    h, m = divmod(m, 60)
   463	    return f"{h}h {m}m {s}s"

   466	def email_skip_reason(sample_mode, skip_email, email_enabled):
   467	    """Return why the email step should be skipped, or None to send.
   468	
   469	    Centralizes the gating so the standalone `cli.py performance` path honors
   470	    the same rules as the orchestrator: sample runs and orchestrator-owned
   471	    delivery (skip_email) are skipped, and EMAIL_ENABLED is the master switch.
   472	    """
   473	    if sample_mode:
   474	        return "sample mode"
   475	    if skip_email:
   476	        return "skip_email"
   477	    if not email_enabled:
   478	        return "EMAIL_ENABLED=False"
   479	    return None

   482	def main(sample_mode=False, refresh=False, skip_email=False):
   483	    """Generate performance reports.
   484	
   485	    Args:
   486	        sample_mode: Sample-mode preview run.
   487	        refresh: Bypass cache.
   488	        skip_email: Suppress the internal email send (set by weekly_report
   489	            so the orchestrator can own email attachments and avoid duplicates).
   490	    """
   491	    global OUTPUT_XLSX, OUTPUT_HTML
   492	    configure_logging()
   493	    os.makedirs(REPORTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
   494	    use_cache = not refresh
   495	    pipeline_start = time.monotonic()
   496	    step_timings = []  # list of (step_name, duration_seconds, detail)
   497	
   498	    if refresh:
   499	        logger.info("Cache bypass enabled (--refresh)")
   500	
   501	    if sample_mode:
   502	        logger.info("=== SAMPLE PREVIEW MODE ===")
   503	        os.makedirs(SAMPLE_REPORTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
   504	        OUTPUT_XLSX = SAMPLE_REPORTS_DIR / "sample_preview.xlsx"
   505	        OUTPUT_HTML = SAMPLE_REPORTS_DIR / "sample_preview.html"
   506	        sample_set = {t.upper() for t in SAMPLE_TICKERS}
   507	    else:
   508	        archive_old_files(REPORTS_DIR, OLD_REPORTS_DIR, TODAY)
   509	
   510	    logger.info("Reading coverage CSV...")
   511	    df = pd.read_csv(CSV_PATH)
   512	
   513	    df_unique = _prepare_universe_rows(df, sample_mode=sample_mode, sample_set=sample_set if sample_mode else None)
   514	    logger.info("Found %s unique tickers", len(df_unique))
   515	
   516	    # Normalize tickers for yfinance
   517	    yf_tickers = [t for t in df_unique["_yf_ticker"].tolist() if t]
   518	    ticker_map = {
   519	        row["_yf_ticker"]: row["Ticker"]
   520	        for row in df_unique[["Ticker", "_yf_ticker"]].to_dict("records")
   521	        if row["_yf_ticker"]
   522	    }
   523	
   524	    logger.info("Downloading data for %s tickers (this may take several minutes)...", len(yf_tickers))
   525	    t0 = time.monotonic()
   526	    all_results = batch_download_prices(yf_tickers, use_cache=use_cache)
   527	
   528	    # FMP fallback for missing US tickers
   529	    fmp_key = API_KEYS.get("FMP_API_KEY")
   530	    if not fmp_key:
   531	        logger.warning("FMP_API_KEY not set — skipping FMP fallback for missing tickers")
   532	    if fmp_key:
   533	        missing = [t for t in yf_tickers if t not in all_results and "." not in t]
   534	        if missing:
   535	            logger.info("Trying FMP API fallback for %s missing US tickers...", len(missing))
   536	            fmp_found = 0
   537	            for t in missing:
   538	                series = try_fmp_historical(t, fmp_key)
   539	                if series is not None:
   540	                    all_results[t] = series
   541	                    fmp_found += 1
   542	            logger.info("FMP resolved %s additional tickers", fmp_found)
   543	
   544	    step_timings.append(("prices", time.monotonic() - t0, f"{len(all_results)}/{len(yf_tickers)} tickers"))
   545	    logger.info("Total tickers with data: %s", len(all_results))
   546	
   547	    # Fetch Finnhub metrics for US tickers (no dot in symbol = likely US)
   548	    finnhub_key = API_KEYS.get("FINNHUB_API_KEY")
   549	    finnhub_data = {}
   550	    t0 = time.monotonic()
   551	    if finnhub_key:
   552	        us_yf_tickers = [t for t in yf_tickers if "." not in t]
   553	        logger.info("Fetching Finnhub fundamentals for %s US tickers...", len(us_yf_tickers))
   554	        finnhub_data = fetch_finnhub_parallel(us_yf_tickers, finnhub_key)
   555	        logger.info("Finnhub returned data for %s tickers", len(finnhub_data))
   556	    step_timings.append(("finnhub", time.monotonic() - t0, f"{len(finnhub_data)} tickers"))
   557	
   558	    # Fetch fundamentals via provider chain (handles FMP/yfinance/AV fallback)
   559	    logger.info("Fetching fundamentals for %s tickers via provider chain...", len(yf_tickers))
   560	    t0 = time.monotonic()
   561	    all_fundamentals, all_is_ttm, all_currencies = fetch_all_fundamentals(

   280	def _load_phase1_tickers():
   281	    """Read all five-state position tickers from exports.
   282	
   283	    Phase 1 of the historical-valuation feature enriches every name with a
   284	    personal trading-state relationship: Portfolio, Researching, Following
   285	    for Interest, Ready to Buy, Ready to Short. Following-for-Interest names
   286	    are included because earnings-season context benefits from the same
   287	    historical-valuation columns the other states rely on.
   288	
   289	    Returns an empty set if the export files are missing — the caller treats
   290	    that as "skip enrichment" and leaves the columns blank.
   291	    """
   292	    from pathlib import Path
   293	    exports_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "exports"
   294	    tickers = set()
   295	    for fname in (
   296	        "portfolio.json",
   297	        "researching.json",
   298	        "following_for_interest.json",
   299	        "ready_to_buy.json",
   300	        "ready_to_short.json",
   301	    ):
   302	        path = exports_dir / fname
   303	        if not path.exists():
   304	            continue
   305	        try:
   306	            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   307	            tickers.update(data.keys())
   308	        except Exception as e:
   309	            logger.warning("Failed to read %s for history universe: %s", fname, e)
   310	    return tickers

   313	def _hist_columns_from_payload(payload):
   314	    """Convert a fetch_history result dict into the history columns.
   315	
   316	    Returns a dict with keys matching `HIST_COLS` (5Y block, 10Y block, and the
   317	    `History Status` marker). Any field that can't be computed (insufficient
   318	    data) is set to None — the Excel writer renders those as N/A. Nothing is
   319	    ever defaulted to 0: a 0 in a P/E-min column would silently corrupt every
   320	    downstream valuation screen.
   321	
   322	    The 5Y and 10Y windows are two slices of the SAME annual series, so the 10Y
   323	    columns add no API cost.
   324	    """
   325	    pe_ttm = payload.get("pe_ttm")
   326	    pe_history = payload.get("pe_history") or []
   327	    evs_history = payload.get("evs_history") or []
   328	
   329	    pe_5 = stats_from_series(pe_history[:5], current=pe_ttm)
   330	    pe_10 = stats_from_series(pe_history[:10], current=pe_ttm)
   331	    # For EV/S vs-avg the "current" comparison uses the existing EV/S (TTM)
   332	    # column populated by the provider chain, which isn't in scope here — pass
   333	    # current=None and let the row-injection step below fill vs_avg_pct.
   334	    evs_5 = stats_from_series(evs_history[:5], current=None)
   335	    evs_10 = stats_from_series(evs_history[:10], current=None)
   336	
   337	    return {
   338	        "P/E (TTM)": pe_ttm,
   339	        "P/E 5Y Avg": pe_5["avg"],
   340	        "P/E 5Y +1σ": pe_5["plus_1sd"],
   341	        "P/E 5Y -1σ": pe_5["minus_1sd"],
   342	        "P/E 5Y Min": pe_5["min"],
   343	        "P/E 5Y Max": pe_5["max"],
   344	        "P/E vs 5Y Avg": pe_5["vs_avg_pct"],
   345	        "EV/S 5Y Avg": evs_5["avg"],
   346	        "EV/S 5Y +1σ": evs_5["plus_1sd"],
   347	        "EV/S 5Y -1σ": evs_5["minus_1sd"],
   348	        "EV/S 5Y Min": evs_5["min"],
   349	        "EV/S 5Y Max": evs_5["max"],
   350	        "EV/S vs 5Y Avg": None,  # filled later once TTM EV/S is in scope
   351	        "P/E 10Y Avg": pe_10["avg"],
   352	        "P/E 10Y +1σ": pe_10["plus_1sd"],
   353	        "P/E 10Y -1σ": pe_10["minus_1sd"],
   354	        "P/E 10Y Min": pe_10["min"],
   355	        "P/E 10Y Max": pe_10["max"],
   356	        "P/E vs 10Y Avg": pe_10["vs_avg_pct"],
   357	        "EV/S 10Y Avg": evs_10["avg"],
   358	        "EV/S 10Y +1σ": evs_10["plus_1sd"],
   359	        "EV/S 10Y -1σ": evs_10["minus_1sd"],
   360	        "EV/S 10Y Min": evs_10["min"],
   361	        "EV/S 10Y Max": evs_10["max"],
   362	        "EV/S vs 10Y Avg": None,  # filled later once TTM EV/S is in scope
   363	        HIST_STATUS_COL: payload.get("status") or STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED,
   364	    }

   367	def _evs_vs_avg_pct(current_evs, evs_history, years=5):
   368	    """Compute (current TTM EV/S - N-year avg) / N-year avg * 100. None-safe."""
   369	    stats = stats_from_series((evs_history or [])[:years], current=current_evs)
   370	    return stats["vs_avg_pct"]

   373	def classify_sector_group(row):
   374	    """Classify a coverage row into a sector group based on Sector (JP) / Subsector (JP)."""
   375	    sector = str(row.get("Sector (JP)", "")).strip()
   376	    subsector = str(row.get("Subsector (JP)", "")).strip()
   377	    if sector in BIOPHARMA_VALUES or subsector in BIOPHARMA_VALUES:
   378	        return "Biopharma"
   379	    if sector in HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES or subsector in HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES:
   380	        return "HC Svcs & MedTech"
   381	    return "Following: Non-HC"

   384	def _split_into_segments(result_df):
   385	    """Split result_df into segment DataFrames keyed by tab name."""
   386	    segments = {"Consolidated": result_df}

   388	    subsector = result_df.get("Subsector (JP)", pd.Series(dtype="object")).fillna("").astype(str).str.strip()
   389	    biopharma_mask = sector.isin(BIOPHARMA_VALUES) | subsector.isin(BIOPHARMA_VALUES)
   390	    hc_svcs_mask = sector.isin(HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES) | subsector.isin(HC_SERVICES_MEDTECH_VALUES)
   391	    non_hc_mask = ~biopharma_mask & ~hc_svcs_mask
   392	    segments["Biopharma"] = result_df[biopharma_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   393	    segments["HC Svcs & MedTech"] = result_df[hc_svcs_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   394	    segments["Following: Non-HC"] = result_df[non_hc_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
   395	    return segments

    20	def batch_download_prices(tickers, start="2015-01-01", batch_size=50, use_cache=True):
    21	    """Download historical close prices from yfinance in batches.
    22	
    23	    Checks same-day cache first. Only downloads uncached tickers.
    24	    Returns dict of {ticker: pd.Series} for tickers with data.
    25	    """
    26	    all_results = {}
    27	    today = date.today().isoformat()
    28	
    29	    # Check cache for same-day price data
    30	    uncached = []
    31	    if use_cache:
    32	        for t in tickers:
    33	            cached = cache_get("prices", f"{t}_{today}", PRICE_CACHE_TTL_HOURS)
    34	            if cached is not None:
    35	                try:
    36	                    series = pd.Series(cached["values"], index=pd.to_datetime(cached["index"]), name=t)
    37	                    all_results[t] = series
    38	                except Exception:
    39	                    uncached.append(t)
    40	            else:
    41	                uncached.append(t)
    42	        if all_results:
    43	            logger.info("Loaded price data for %d/%d tickers from cache", len(all_results), len(tickers))
    44	    else:
    45	        uncached = list(tickers)
    46	
    47	    if not uncached:
    48	        logger.info("All %d tickers served from price cache", len(tickers))
    49	        return all_results
    50	
    51	    total_batches = (len(uncached) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size
    52	
    53	    newly_fetched = {}
    54	    for i in range(0, len(uncached), batch_size):
    55	        batch = uncached[i:i + batch_size]
    56	        batch_num = i // batch_size + 1
    57	        logger.info("Batch %s/%s (%s tickers)...", batch_num, total_batches, len(batch))
    58	        try:
    59	            data = yf.download(
    60	                batch,
    61	                start=start,
    62	                auto_adjust=True,
    63	                progress=False,
    64	                threads=True,
    65	            )
    66	            if data.empty:
    67	                continue
    68	            close = data["Close"]
    69	            if isinstance(close, pd.Series):
    70	                t = batch[0]
    71	                series = close.dropna()
    72	                all_results[t] = series
    73	                newly_fetched[t] = series
    74	            else:
    75	                for t in batch:
    76	                    if t in close.columns:
    77	                        series = close[t].dropna()
    78	                        if len(series) > 0:
    79	                            all_results[t] = series
    80	                            newly_fetched[t] = series
    81	        except Exception as e:
    82	            logger.warning("Error in batch %s: %s", batch_num, e)
    83	            continue
    84	
    85	    # Cache newly fetched price data for same-day reruns
    86	    if use_cache and newly_fetched:
    87	        for t, series in newly_fetched.items():
    88	            try:
    89	                cache_set("prices", f"{t}_{today}", {
    90	                    "index": [d.isoformat() for d in series.index],
    91	                    "values": series.tolist(),
    92	                })
    93	            except Exception:
    94	                pass  # Don't let cache errors break the pipeline
    95	
    96	    logger.info("Price data: %d from cache, %d newly fetched, %d total",
    97	                len(all_results) - len(newly_fetched), len(newly_fetched), len(all_results))
    98	    return all_results

   101	@retry_on_failure(max_retries=2, base_delay=1.0, logger_name="providers.yfinance")
   102	def _fetch_ticker_info(yf_ticker):
   103	    """Fetch yfinance Ticker.info with retry on transient failures."""
   104	    return yf.Ticker(yf_ticker).info
   105	
   106	
   107	def fetch_fundamentals(yf_ticker, finnhub_metrics=None, use_cache=True):
   108	    """Fetch fundamental data from yfinance, enriched with Finnhub for US tickers.
   109	
   110	    Returns (result, is_ttm, currency) where is_ttm tracks whether Finnhub TTM YoY
   111	    data was used for Rev Grw and EPS Grw.
   112	    """
   113	    result = {col: None for col in FUND_COLS + VAL_COLS}
   114	    is_ttm = {"Rev Grw": False, "EPS Grw": False}
   115	    currency = ""
   116	
   117	    # Check cache for yfinance fundamentals (before Finnhub enrichment)
   118	    # ⛑ `yf2_` (2026-09-08). An entry cached under `yf_` predates `_valuation`
   119	    # and therefore carries no primitives -- which the new rule reads as "EV is
   120	    # unprovable" and blanks. Bumping the namespace refetches rather than
   121	    # publishing a day of blank EV columns off a stale cache shape.
   122	    cache_key = f"yf2_{yf_ticker}"
   123	    if use_cache:
   124	        cached = cache_get("fundamentals", cache_key, FUND_CACHE_TTL_HOURS)
   125	        if cached is not None:
   126	            result = cached.get("result", result)
   127	            currency = cached.get("currency", currency)
   128	            # Still apply Finnhub enrichment on top of cached yfinance data
   129	            if finnhub_metrics:
   130	                fh_rev = finnhub_metrics.get("revenueGrowthTTMYoy")
   131	                if fh_rev is not None:
   132	                    result["Rev Grw"] = fh_rev
   133	                    is_ttm["Rev Grw"] = True
   134	                fh_eps = finnhub_metrics.get("epsGrowthTTMYoy")
   135	                if fh_eps is not None:
   136	                    result["EPS Grw"] = fh_eps
   137	                    is_ttm["EPS Grw"] = True
   138	                fh_peg = finnhub_metrics.get("pegTTM")
   139	                if fh_peg is not None:
   140	                    result["PEG"] = fh_peg
   141	            return result, is_ttm, currency
   142	
   143	    try:
   144	        info = _fetch_ticker_info(yf_ticker)
   145	        if not info:
   146	            return result, is_ttm, currency
   147	
   148	        result["Mkt Cap"] = info.get("marketCap")
   149	        result["Enterprise Value"] = info.get("enterpriseValue")
   150	        result["Price"] = info.get("currentPrice") or info.get("regularMarketPrice")
   151	
   152	        # ⛑ `ev - mc` IS NET DEBT IN THE REPORTING CURRENCY, and the comment
   153	        # block below used to label it the quote currency. Yahoo's EV is
   154	        # `marketCap` (quote) plus `totalDebt - totalCash` (reporting) summed as
   155	        # if one unit, so the subtraction returns exactly the reporting-currency
   156	        # leg back. For Novo that is DKK 95bn published as USD 95bn.
   157	        #
   158	        # It is kept ONLY so `_is_success` and `_merge_partial` behave as before;
   159	        # `reporting.generate` OVERWRITES both from `_valuation` below. Do not
   160	        # read `Enterprise Value` or `Net Debt` off this dict and treat them as
   161	        # convertible on one rate -- that is the bug.
   162	        ev = info.get("enterpriseValue")
   163	        mc = info.get("marketCap")
   164	        if ev is not None and mc is not None:
   165	            result["Net Debt"] = ev - mc
   166	        else:
   167	            result["Net Debt"] = None
   168	
   169	        # ⛑ THE PRIMITIVES, each carrying ONE known currency. This is what makes
   170	        # a correct EV computable downstream, where the FX rates live. Without
   171	        # it the report can only convert a number that is in no currency.
   172	        result["_valuation"] = {
   173	            "currency": info.get("currency"),
   174	            "financialCurrency": info.get("financialCurrency"),
   175	            "marketCap": info.get("marketCap"),
   176	            "totalDebt": info.get("totalDebt"),
   177	            "totalCash": info.get("totalCash"),
   178	            "totalRevenue": info.get("totalRevenue"),
   179	            "ebitda": info.get("ebitda"),
   180	        }
   181	
   182	        result["Fwd P/E"] = info.get("forwardPE")
   183	        result["EV/EBITDA"] = info.get("enterpriseToEbitda")
   184	        result["EV/S"] = info.get("enterpriseToRevenue")
   185	
   186	        # ⛑ THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY "Mkt Cap / EV / Net Debt are price-derived,
   187	        # so they are in the QUOTE currency". That is true of `Mkt Cap` ONLY, and
   188	        # the sentence is what made the other two look safe to convert on one
   189	        # rate for months. EV is `Mkt Cap` (quote) + net debt (reporting) summed
   190	        # raw -- no currency at all -- and `Net Debt` is purely reporting.
   191	        #
   192	        # `currency` is the QUOTE currency and is correct for `Mkt Cap` and
   193	        # `Price`: an ADR like NVO quotes USD while reporting DKK, so using the
   194	        # reporting currency here would mis-convert the cap. The reporting
   195	        # currency is carried separately in `_valuation` for the fields that
   196	        # actually need it. NOTE: currency is cached alongside fundamentals, so a
   197	        # re-cache (`--refresh`, or 24h TTL expiry) is needed for existing rows.
   198	        currency = info.get("currency") or info.get("financialCurrency") or ""
   199	
   200	        gm = info.get("grossMargins")
   201	        result["Gross Mgn"] = gm * 100 if gm is not None else None
   202	        om = info.get("operatingMargins")
   203	        result["Op Mgn"] = om * 100 if om is not None else None
   204	        roe = info.get("returnOnEquity")
   205	        result["ROE"] = roe * 100 if roe is not None else None
   206	
   207	        rev_grw = info.get("revenueGrowth")
   208	        result["Rev Grw"] = rev_grw * 100 if rev_grw is not None else None
   209	        eps_grw = info.get("earningsGrowth")
   210	        result["EPS Grw"] = eps_grw * 100 if eps_grw is not None else None
   211	
   212	        result["PEG"] = info.get("pegRatio")
   213	
   214	        # Cache yfinance data before Finnhub enrichment
   215	        if use_cache and result.get("Mkt Cap") is not None:
   216	            cache_set("fundamentals", cache_key, {"result": result.copy(), "currency": currency})
   217	    except Exception as e:
   218	        log_exception(logger, f"Fundamental lookup failed for {yf_ticker}", e)
   219	
   220	    if finnhub_metrics:
   221	        fh_rev = finnhub_metrics.get("revenueGrowthTTMYoy")
   222	        if fh_rev is not None:
   223	            result["Rev Grw"] = fh_rev
   224	            is_ttm["Rev Grw"] = True
   225	        fh_eps = finnhub_metrics.get("epsGrowthTTMYoy")
   226	        if fh_eps is not None:
   227	            result["EPS Grw"] = fh_eps
   228	            is_ttm["EPS Grw"] = True
   229	        fh_peg = finnhub_metrics.get("pegTTM")
   230	        if fh_peg is not None:
   231	            result["PEG"] = fh_peg
   232	
   233	    return result, is_ttm, currency
   234	
   235	
   236	def fetch_fundamentals_parallel(yf_tickers, finnhub_data=None, max_workers=10, use_cache=True):
   237	    """Fetch fundamentals for a list of tickers in parallel.
   238	
   239	    Returns (all_fundamentals, all_is_ttm, all_currencies) dicts keyed by yf_ticker.
   240	    """
   241	    if finnhub_data is None:
   242	        finnhub_data = {}
   243	
   244	    all_fundamentals = {}
   245	    all_is_ttm = {}
   246	    all_currencies = {}
   247	    total = len(yf_tickers)
   248	
   249	    def _fetch_one(yf_t):
   250	        fh = finnhub_data.get(yf_t)
   251	        return yf_t, fetch_fundamentals(yf_t, finnhub_metrics=fh, use_cache=use_cache)
   252	
   253	    completed = 0
   254	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   255	        futures = {executor.submit(_fetch_one, t): t for t in yf_tickers}
   256	        for future in as_completed(futures):
   257	            yf_t, (fund_result, is_ttm, currency) = future.result()
   258	            all_fundamentals[yf_t] = fund_result
   259	            all_is_ttm[yf_t] = is_ttm
   260	            all_currencies[yf_t] = currency
   261	            completed += 1
   262	            if completed % 100 == 0:
   263	                logger.info("Fundamentals %s/%s...", completed, total)
   264	
   265	    return all_fundamentals, all_is_ttm, all_currencies
     1	"""Provider chain — thin coordinator for fundamentals fallback and merging.
     2	
     3	Responsibilities:
     4	  - Per-ticker fallback coordination (primary → secondary → AV)
     5	  - Field-level merging of partial results
     6	  - Fallback rate logging by exchange
     7	
     8	Does NOT own parsing (that stays in each provider) or orchestration
     9	(that stays in generate.py).
    10	"""
    11	
    12	from collections import defaultdict
    13	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
    14	
    15	from config import PROVIDER_PRIORITY, API_KEYS
    16	from reporting.calcs import FUND_COLS, VAL_COLS
    17	from logging_utils import get_logger, log_exception
    18	from providers.fmp_provider import fetch_fundamentals as fmp_fetch
    19	from providers.yfinance_provider import fetch_fundamentals as yf_fetch
    20	from providers.alphavantage_provider import fetch_fundamentals as av_fetch
    21	
    22	logger = get_logger("providers.chain")
    23	
    24	
    25	def _is_success(result):
    26	    """Multi-field success rule: Mkt Cap + currency + at least one valuation/quality field."""
    27	    if result.get("Mkt Cap") is None:
    28	        return False
    29	    quality_fields = [
    30	        "Enterprise Value", "Fwd P/E", "EV/EBITDA", "EV/S",
    31	        "Gross Mgn", "Op Mgn", "ROE", "Rev Grw", "EPS Grw",
    32	    ]
    33	    return any(result.get(f) is not None for f in quality_fields)
    34	
    35	
    36	def _merge_partial(base, overlay):
    37	    """Merge overlay fields into base where base has None values.
    38	
    39	    Does not overwrite existing non-None values.
    40	    """
    41	    for key, val in overlay.items():
    42	        if val is not None and base.get(key) is None:
    43	            base[key] = val
    44	    return base
    45	
    46	
    47	def fetch_fundamentals_with_fallback(
    48	    ticker,
    49	    finnhub_metrics=None,
    50	    use_cache=True,
    51	    priority=None,
    52	    *,
    53	    _fmp_api_key=None,
    54	    _av_api_key=None,
    55	):
    56	    """Fetch fundamentals for a single ticker with fallback chain.
    57	
    58	    Args:
    59	        ticker: The ticker symbol (yfinance-normalized for yf, raw for FMP).
    60	        finnhub_metrics: Optional Finnhub metrics dict for TTM overlay.
    61	        use_cache: Whether to use cache.
    62	        priority: Override PROVIDER_PRIORITY ("fmp_first" or "yf_first").
    63	        _fmp_api_key: FMP API key (defaults to API_KEYS).
    64	        _av_api_key: AV API key (defaults to API_KEYS).
    65	
    66	    Returns:
    67	        (result, is_ttm, currency, provider_used) where provider_used is
    68	        "fmp", "yfinance", "alphavantage", or "none".
    69	    """
    70	    effective_priority = priority or PROVIDER_PRIORITY
    71	    fmp_key = _fmp_api_key if _fmp_api_key is not None else API_KEYS.get("FMP_API_KEY", "")
    72	    av_key = _av_api_key if _av_api_key is not None else API_KEYS.get("ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY", "")
    73	
    74	    result = {col: None for col in FUND_COLS + VAL_COLS}
    75	    is_ttm = {"Rev Grw": False, "EPS Grw": False}
    76	    currency = ""
    77	    provider_used = "none"
    78	
    79	    if effective_priority == "fmp_first":
    80	        providers = [
    81	            ("fmp", lambda: fmp_fetch(ticker, fmp_key, use_cache=use_cache)),
    82	            ("yfinance", lambda: yf_fetch(ticker, finnhub_metrics=None, use_cache=use_cache)),
    83	        ]
    84	    else:
    85	        providers = [
    86	            ("yfinance", lambda: yf_fetch(ticker, finnhub_metrics=None, use_cache=use_cache)),
    87	            ("fmp", lambda: fmp_fetch(ticker, fmp_key, use_cache=use_cache)),
    88	        ]
    89	
    90	    for name, fetcher in providers:
    91	        try:
    92	            res, ttm, cur = fetcher()
    93	        except Exception as e:
    94	            log_exception(logger, f"{name} fundamentals failed for {ticker}", e)
    95	            continue
    96	
    97	        if provider_used == "none":
    98	            # First provider to return anything with Mkt Cap
    99	            if res.get("Mkt Cap") is not None:
   100	                result = res
   101	                is_ttm = ttm
   102	                currency = cur
   103	                provider_used = name
   104	                if _is_success(res):
   105	                    break
   106	            # else: complete miss, try next
   107	        else:
   108	            # We already have partial from primary — merge secondary into it
   109	            if res.get("Mkt Cap") is not None:
   110	                _merge_partial(result, res)
   111	                # Don't overwrite currency from primary
   112	            break  # We've tried both, done
   113	
   114	    # If still not successful after both, no further merge needed here
   115	    # (AV fallback below handles the final attempt)
   116	
   117	    # AlphaVantage as final fallback if still not successful
   118	    if not _is_success(result) and av_key:
   119	        # ⛑ A SUFFIXED SYMBOL IS NEVER SENT HERE, AND IS NEVER STRIPPED TO FIT.
   120	        # This used to read `av_symbol = ticker.split(".")[0]`, which turns
   121	        # `MED.SW` (Medartis, SIX) into `MED` and asks AlphaVantage about
   122	        # MEDIFAST — then `_merge_partial` folds the namesake's market cap,
   123	        # margins and growth into the row with no currency guard. That is the
   124	        # wrong-company bug class this repo has repaired three times, except
   125	        # reached from a row whose ticker is entirely CORRECT, so no amount of
   126	        # fixing the universe prevents it.
   127	        # AlphaVantage is a US-symbol service and a foreign line simply has no
   128	        # answer here. Skipping yields a missing value, which is visible; the
   129	        # strip yielded a confident wrong one, which is not.
   130	        if "." in ticker or " " in ticker:
   131	            logger.debug(
   132	                "AlphaVantage fallback skipped for %s: suffixed/foreign symbol, "
   133	                "and stripping the suffix would query a different issuer", ticker)
   134	        else:
   135	            try:
   136	                av_data = av_fetch(ticker, av_key, use_cache=use_cache)
   137	                if av_data and av_data.get("Mkt Cap") is not None:
   138	                    _merge_partial(result, av_data)
   139	                    if provider_used == "none":
   140	                        provider_used = "alphavantage"
   141	            except Exception as e:
   142	                log_exception(logger, f"AlphaVantage fallback failed for {ticker}", e)
   143	
   144	    # Finnhub TTM overlay always wins for growth + PEG
   145	    if finnhub_metrics:
   146	        fh_rev = finnhub_metrics.get("revenueGrowthTTMYoy")
   147	        if fh_rev is not None:
   148	            result["Rev Grw"] = fh_rev
   149	            is_ttm["Rev Grw"] = True
   150	        fh_eps = finnhub_metrics.get("epsGrowthTTMYoy")
   151	        if fh_eps is not None:
   152	            result["EPS Grw"] = fh_eps
   153	            is_ttm["EPS Grw"] = True
   154	        fh_peg = finnhub_metrics.get("pegTTM")
   155	        if fh_peg is not None:
   156	            result["PEG"] = fh_peg
   157	
   158	    return result, is_ttm, currency, provider_used
   159	
   160	
   161	def fetch_all_fundamentals(
   162	    tickers,
   163	    finnhub_data=None,
   164	    max_workers=10,
   165	    use_cache=True,
   166	    priority=None,
   167	):
   168	    """Fetch fundamentals for all tickers with fallback chain (parallel).
   169	
   170	    Returns (all_fundamentals, all_is_ttm, all_currencies) matching the
   171	    contract expected by generate.py.
   172	
   173	    Also logs fallback rates by exchange suffix for monitoring.
   174	    """
   175	    if finnhub_data is None:
   176	        finnhub_data = {}
   177	
   178	    all_fundamentals = {}
   179	    all_is_ttm = {}
   180	    all_currencies = {}
   181	    provider_counts = defaultdict(int)
   182	    exchange_fallbacks = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
   183	
   184	    def _fetch_one(t):
   185	        fh = finnhub_data.get(t)
   186	        return t, fetch_fundamentals_with_fallback(
   187	            t, finnhub_metrics=fh, use_cache=use_cache, priority=priority
   188	        )
   189	
   190	    completed = 0
   191	    total = len(tickers)
   192	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   193	        futures = {executor.submit(_fetch_one, t): t for t in tickers}
   194	        for future in as_completed(futures):
   195	            try:
   196	                t, (fund_result, is_ttm, currency, provider_used) = future.result()
   197	            except Exception as e:
   198	                t = futures[future]
   199	                log_exception(logger, f"Provider chain failed for {t}", e)
   200	                fund_result = {col: None for col in FUND_COLS + VAL_COLS}
   201	                is_ttm = {"Rev Grw": False, "EPS Grw": False}
   202	                currency = ""
   203	                provider_used = "none"
   204	
   205	            all_fundamentals[t] = fund_result
   206	            all_is_ttm[t] = is_ttm
   207	            all_currencies[t] = currency
   208	            provider_counts[provider_used] += 1
   209	
   210	            # Track fallback by exchange suffix (for international monitoring)
   211	            suffix = t.split(".")[-1] if "." in t else "US"
   212	            exchange_fallbacks[suffix][provider_used] += 1
   213	
   214	            completed += 1
   215	            if completed % 100 == 0:
   216	                logger.info("Fundamentals %s/%s...", completed, total)
   217	
   218	    # Log summary
   219	    logger.info(
   220	        "Provider chain complete: %s",
   221	        ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(provider_counts.items())),
   222	    )
   223	    for suffix, counts in sorted(exchange_fallbacks.items()):
   224	        if suffix != "US":
   225	            logger.info(
   226	                "  Exchange .%s: %s",
   227	                suffix,
   228	                ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(counts.items())),
   229	            )
   230	
   231	    return all_fundamentals, all_is_ttm, all_currencies
     1	"""File-based cache for external data.
     2	
     3	Stores JSON files in cache/<namespace>/<key>.json with timestamps.
     4	Supports TTL-based expiry and manual clearing.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import json
     8	import shutil
     9	from datetime import datetime, timezone
    10	from pathlib import Path
    11	
    12	from config import CACHE_DIR
    13	from logging_utils import get_logger
    14	
    15	logger = get_logger("cache")
    16	
    17	
    18	def _cache_path(namespace, key):
    19	    """Return the path for a cache entry."""
    20	    safe_key = key.replace("/", "_").replace("\\", "_").replace(":", "_")
    21	    return CACHE_DIR / namespace / f"{safe_key}.json"
    22	
    23	
    24	def cache_get(namespace, key, max_age_hours):
    25	    """Read from cache if not expired.
    26	
    27	    Returns the cached data, or None if missing/expired/corrupt.
    28	    """
    29	    path = _cache_path(namespace, key)
    30	    if not path.exists():
    31	        return None
    32	
    33	    try:
    34	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    35	            entry = json.load(f)
    36	
    37	        cached_at = datetime.fromisoformat(entry["_cached_at"])
    38	        age_hours = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - cached_at).total_seconds() / 3600
    39	
    40	        if age_hours > max_age_hours:
    41	            logger.debug("Cache expired for %s/%s (%.1fh > %.1fh)", namespace, key, age_hours, max_age_hours)
    42	            return None
    43	
    44	        return entry["data"]
    45	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
    46	        logger.warning("Corrupt cache entry %s/%s: %s", namespace, key, e)
    47	        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    48	        return None
    49	
    50	
    51	def cache_set(namespace, key, data):
    52	    """Write data to cache with current timestamp."""
    53	    path = _cache_path(namespace, key)
    54	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    55	
    56	    entry = {
    57	        "_cached_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    58	        "data": data,
    59	    }
    60	    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    61	        json.dump(entry, f, default=str)
    62	
    63	
    64	def cache_clear(namespace=None):
    65	    """Delete cached files. Returns count of files deleted.
    66	
    67	    If namespace is None, clears all namespaces.
    68	    """
    69	    if not CACHE_DIR.exists():
    70	        return 0
    71	
    72	    count = 0
    73	    if namespace:
    74	        target = CACHE_DIR / namespace
    75	        if target.exists():
    76	            for f in target.glob("*.json"):
    77	                f.unlink()
    78	                count += 1
    79	            logger.info("Cleared %d cache entries from %s", count, namespace)
    80	    else:
    81	        for ns_dir in CACHE_DIR.iterdir():
    82	            if ns_dir.is_dir():
    83	                for f in ns_dir.glob("*.json"):
    84	                    f.unlink()
    85	                    count += 1
    86	        logger.info("Cleared %d cache entries from all namespaces", count)
    87	    return count
    88	
    89	
    90	def cache_stats():
    91	    """Return dict of {namespace: entry_count} for diagnostics."""
    92	    stats = {}
    93	    if not CACHE_DIR.exists():
    94	        return stats
    95	    for ns_dir in CACHE_DIR.iterdir():
    96	        if ns_dir.is_dir():
    97	            stats[ns_dir.name] = len(list(ns_dir.glob("*.json")))
    98	    return stats
     1	"""Movers report orchestration — the connective tissue between the
     2	performance snapshot, the movers module, and the delivery surfaces (file,
     3	email, Slack).
     4	
     5	Used by both ``cli.py movers`` (ad-hoc invocation) and ``weekly_report.py``
     6	(automated run after the performance step).
     7	"""
     8	
     9	from __future__ import annotations
    10	
    11	import os
    12	from pathlib import Path
    13	
    14	import pandas as pd
    15	
    16	from config import (
    17	    API_KEYS,
    18	    CACHE_DIR,
    19	    REPORTS_DIR,
    20	    TODAY,
    21	    MOVERS_ABS_THRESHOLD_PCT,
    22	    MOVERS_ZSCORE_THRESHOLD,
    23	    MOVERS_MIN_PEER_COUNT,
    24	    MOVERS_MAX_FLAGGED,
    25	    MOVERS_LLM_MODEL,
    26	)
    27	from logging_utils import get_logger
    28	from reporting import movers
    29	from reporting.slack import send_slack_notification
    30	
    31	logger = get_logger("movers_runner")
    32	
    33	
    34	def _load_perf_snapshot(snapshot_date: str) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    35	    """Load the perf snapshot pickle written by reporting/generate.py.
    36	
    37	    Returns None if the snapshot doesn't exist — caller decides whether to
    38	    error or fall through to a price-only fallback.
    39	    """
    40	    path = CACHE_DIR / "perf" / f"perf_df_{snapshot_date}.pkl"
    41	    if not path.exists():
    42	        logger.warning("No perf snapshot at %s", path)
    43	        return None
    44	    try:
    45	        df = pd.read_pickle(path)
    46	        logger.info("Loaded perf snapshot: %s (%d rows)", path, len(df))
    47	        return df
    48	    except Exception as e:
    49	        logger.warning("Failed to load perf snapshot %s: %s", path, e)
    50	        return None
    51	
    52	
    53	def run(
    54	    snapshot_date: str | None = None,
    55	    skip_news: bool = False,
    56	    skip_slack: bool = False,
    57	) -> dict:
    58	    """Generate the movers report and write artifacts to ``reports/``.
    59	
    60	    Args:
    61	        snapshot_date: Date string (YYYY-MM-DD) for the perf snapshot to
    62	            load. Defaults to TODAY.
    63	        skip_news: Skip Finnhub news + Anthropic summary enrichment.
    64	        skip_slack: Skip the Slack post even if a webhook is configured.
    65	
    66	    Returns dict with: count, html_path, md_path, slack_posted, error.
    67	    """
    68	    snap_date = snapshot_date or TODAY
    69	    result = {
    70	        "count": 0,
    71	        "html_path": None,
    72	        "md_path": None,
    73	        "slack_posted": False,
    74	        "error": None,
    75	    }
    76	
    77	    df = _load_perf_snapshot(snap_date)
    78	    if df is None or df.empty:
    79	        msg = f"No perf snapshot for {snap_date}; run `cli.py performance` first."
    80	        logger.warning(msg)
    81	        result["error"] = msg
    82	        return result
    83	
    84	    finnhub_key = "" if skip_news else (API_KEYS.get("FINNHUB_API_KEY") or "")
    85	    anthropic_key = "" if skip_news else (API_KEYS.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") or os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", ""))
    86	    if not skip_news and not anthropic_key:
    87	        logger.info("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set; movers report will skip LLM 'why' summaries")
    88	
    89	    bundle = movers.run(
    90	        perf_df=df,
    91	        today=snap_date,
    92	        finnhub_key=finnhub_key,
    93	        anthropic_key=anthropic_key,
    94	        abs_threshold_pct=MOVERS_ABS_THRESHOLD_PCT,
    95	        z_threshold=MOVERS_ZSCORE_THRESHOLD,
    96	        min_peer_count=MOVERS_MIN_PEER_COUNT,
    97	        max_flagged=MOVERS_MAX_FLAGGED,
    98	        llm_model=MOVERS_LLM_MODEL,
    99	    )
   100	    result["count"] = bundle["count"]
   101	
   102	    html_path = Path(REPORTS_DIR) / f"coverage_movers_{snap_date}.html"
   103	    md_path = Path(REPORTS_DIR) / f"coverage_movers_{snap_date}.md"
   104	    html_path.write_text(bundle["html"], encoding="utf-8")
   105	    md_path.write_text(bundle["md"], encoding="utf-8")
   106	    result["html_path"] = str(html_path)
   107	    result["md_path"] = str(md_path)
   108	    logger.info("Wrote %s and %s", html_path, md_path)
   109	
   110	    # Slack — non-fatal if it fails.
   111	    if not skip_slack:
   112	        webhook = API_KEYS.get("SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL") or os.environ.get("SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL", "")
   113	        if webhook:
   114	            try:
   115	                ok = send_slack_notification(webhook, bundle["slack"])
   116	                result["slack_posted"] = bool(ok)
   117	            except Exception as e:

   119	        else:
   120	            logger.info("Skipping Slack post — no SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL set")

   122	    return result
