   144	
   145	def _parse_price(raw, field):
   146	    if raw is None or str(raw).strip() == "":
   147	        return None
   148	    try:
   149	        val = float(str(raw).strip())
   150	    except ValueError as e:
   151	        raise PositionsError(f"{field} must be a number, got {raw!r}") from e
   152	    if val <= 0:
   153	        raise PositionsError(f"{field} must be positive, got {val}")
   154	    return val
   155	
   156	
   157	def _parse_shares(raw, field):
   158	    """Share counts are FRACTIONAL and must not be rounded.
   159	
   160	    This was `_parse_int` doing `int(float(x))`, which silently TRUNCATED: the real
   161	    book carries FMS 452.656, PACS 277.893, CI 40.532, AAPL 13.036. While the column
   162	    was reserved-and-blank that cost nothing; the moment it is filled from the broker
   163	    feed it would publish 452 shares for a 452.656 holding -- a wrong number that
   164	    looks entirely plausible. Non-negative rather than strictly positive (unlike
   165	    `_parse_price`), because zero shares is expressible even though the feed omits
   166	    such rows.
   167	    """
   168	    if raw is None or str(raw).strip() == "":
   169	        return None
   170	    try:
   171	        val = float(str(raw).strip())
   172	    except ValueError as e:
   173	        raise PositionsError(f"{field} must be a number, got {raw!r}") from e
   174	    if val < 0:
   175	        raise PositionsError(f"{field} must be non-negative, got {val}")
   176	    return val
   177	
   178	
   179	def load(path=POSITIONS_PATH):
   180	    """Read the positions CSV and return a list of dicts.
   181	
   182	    Returns an empty list if the file does not exist. Does NOT validate
   183	    against the universe — use `validate()` for that.
   184	    """
   185	    path = Path(path)
   186	    if not path.exists():
   187	        return []
   188	    entries = []
   189	    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   190	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
   191	        for row in reader:
   192	            ticker = (row.get("Ticker") or "").strip()
   193	            if not ticker:
   194	                continue
   195	            entry = {
   196	                "Ticker": ticker,
   197	                "Position Date": (row.get("Position Date") or "").strip(),
   198	                "First Buy Date": (row.get("First Buy Date") or "").strip(),
   199	                "Average Cost": _parse_price(row.get("Average Cost"), "Average Cost"),
   200	                "Shares": _parse_shares(row.get("Shares"), "Shares"),
   201	                "Notes": (row.get("Notes") or "").strip(),
   202	                # Derived columns. Absent in a pre-2026-08-23 file, which reads as
   203	                # "" -- NOT as "N". A missing key is not a value: `held.plan_sync`
   204	                # treats only an explicit "Y" as held, so an unmigrated file
   205	                # promotes rather than mass-demoting on the first run.
   206	                "Held": (row.get("Held") or "").strip(),
   207	                "Held As Of": (row.get("Held As Of") or "").strip(),
   208	                "Previously Held": (row.get("Previously Held") or "").strip(),
   209	                "Held Until": (row.get("Held Until") or "").strip(),
   210	            }
   211	            legacy = (row.get("Position") or "").strip()
   212	            has_any_flag = any((row.get(f) or "").strip() for f in STATE_FLAGS)
   213	            for flag in STATE_FLAGS:
   214	                v = (row.get(flag) or "").strip().upper()
   215	                if not has_any_flag and legacy == flag:
   216	                    # UPGRADE-ON-READ from a pre-flags file. Only when NO flag column
   217	                    # carries anything -- otherwise a row deliberately cleared of a
   218	                    # flag would have it silently restored from the stale `Position`
   219	                    # mirror on every load, and the mirror would quietly become the
   220	                    # store again.
   221	                    v = "Y"
   222	                entry[flag] = v
   223	            # Carry the derived mirror in memory too, so `filter_by_position` and
   224	            # every caller that reads `entry["Position"]` keeps working against a
   225	            # value that is always consistent with the flags. Writing it here (not
   226	            # copying the file's cell) is what stops a stale mirror being believed.
   227	            entry["Position"] = published_position(entry)
   228	            entries.append(entry)
   229	    return entries
   230	
   231	
   232	def is_held(entry):
   233	    """True when the BROKERS report this name as held. The only ownership test."""
   234	    return (entry.get("Held") or "").strip().upper() == "Y"
   235	
   236	
   237	def has_state(entry, flag):
   238	    """True when this row carries the named intent flag."""
   239	    return (entry.get(flag) or "").strip().upper() == "Y"
   240	
   241	
   242	def published_position(entry):
   243	    """Collapse ownership + the intent flags into the single legacy `Position`.
   244	
   245	    The stored truth is now one flag per state plus the derived `Held` column, but
   246	    the published artifacts must not move: ~8 sibling repos read `position`, and
   247	    `earnings_agent` subgroups on this very field. So this is the ONE place that
   248	    decides what a row is called, and every export goes through it -- portfolio.json
   249	    (weekly_universe), the sigma-alert payloads (reporting/sigma_export), and the
   250	    joined positions CSV. Three copies of the rule would be three chances for them
   251	    to disagree about what the fleet owns.
   252	
   253	    Ownership wins outright: if the brokers say you hold it, that is what it is,
   254	    whatever you also intend. Below that, `STATE_FLAGS` order applies -- and a name
   255	    carrying two flags is real (a bellwether you have started underwriting), which
   256	    is exactly why the flags are the store and this scalar is only a projection.
   257	    """
   258	    if is_held(entry):
   259	        return "Portfolio"
   260	    for flag in STATE_FLAGS:
   261	        if has_state(entry, flag):
   262	            return flag
   263	    return ""
   264	
   265	
   266	def filter_by_position(entries, position):
   267	    """Return entries where Position matches (e.g. "Portfolio" or "Researching")."""
   268	    return [e for e in entries if e.get("Position") == position]

   270	
   271	def save(entries, path=POSITIONS_PATH):
   272	    """Write entries back to the positions CSV, sorted by ticker."""
   273	    path = Path(path)
   274	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   275	    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e["Ticker"].upper())
   276	    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   277	        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=POSITIONS_COLUMNS)
   278	        writer.writeheader()
   279	        for e in sorted_entries:
   280	            writer.writerow({
   281	                "Ticker": e["Ticker"],
   282	                "Position Date": e.get("Position Date", ""),
   283	                "First Buy Date": e.get("First Buy Date", ""),
   284	                "Average Cost": "" if e.get("Average Cost") is None else e["Average Cost"],
   285	                "Shares": "" if e.get("Shares") is None else e["Shares"],
   286	                "Notes": e.get("Notes", ""),
   287	                "Held": e.get("Held", ""),
   288	                "Held As Of": e.get("Held As Of", ""),
   289	                "Previously Held": e.get("Previously Held", ""),
   290	                "Held Until": e.get("Held Until", ""),
   291	                **{f: (e.get(f) or "") for f in STATE_FLAGS},
   292	                # DERIVED MIRROR, written so anything still reading `Position`
   293	                # keeps working. Never read it back as the store -- `load` only
   294	                # trusts it when no flag column exists at all.
   295	                "Position": published_position(e),
   296	            })
   297	
   298	
   299	def validate(entries, universe_csv_path=CSV_PATH):
   300	    """Check that entries are a strict subset of the coverage universe, every
   301	    Position value is valid, and each ticker's universe row has the metadata
   302	    fields downstream consumers need.
   303	
   304	    Returns (errors, warnings) — lists of strings. `errors` is non-empty when
   305	    the file cannot be used as-is.
   306	    """
   307	    errors = []
   308	    warnings = []
   309	    universe_rows = _load_universe_rows(universe_csv_path)
   310	
   311	    seen = set()
   312	    for e in entries:
   313	        t = e["Ticker"]
   314	        if t in seen:
   315	            errors.append(f"duplicate ticker: {t}")
   316	            continue
   317	        seen.add(t)
   318	
   319	        # Validate the FLAGS, which are the store. `Position` is a derived mirror
   320	        # and is legitimately empty on a held row that carries no intent -- which
   321	        # is the normal shape for something you simply own.
   322	        for flag in STATE_FLAGS:
   323	            v = (e.get(flag) or "").strip().upper()
   324	            if v not in ("", "Y", "N"):
   325	                errors.append(f"{t}: {flag} must be Y, N or blank, got {e.get(flag)!r}")
   326	        if not is_held(e) and not any(has_state(e, f) for f in STATE_FLAGS):
   327	            # A row that is neither held nor carries any intent is a row with no
   328	            # reason to be in this file. Reported rather than dropped: it is far
   329	            # likelier to be a flag someone cleared by mistake than a deliberate
   330	            # blank, and silently removing coverage is the unrecoverable direction.
   331	            errors.append(
   332	                f"{t}: not held and carries no intent flag "
   333	                f"({', '.join(STATE_FLAGS)}) - it has no reason to be in this file"
   334	            )
   335	
   336	        row = universe_rows.get(t)
   337	        if row is None:
   338	            errors.append(
   339	                f"{t} is not in the coverage universe — add it via discovery first"
   340	            )
   341	        else:
   342	            missing = [
   343	                f for f in REQUIRED_METADATA_FIELDS
   344	                if not (row.get(f) or "").strip()
   345	            ]
   346	            if missing:
   347	                errors.append(
   348	                    f"{t}: missing universe metadata for {', '.join(missing)} — "
   349	                    f"fix the universe CSV row before using this ticker"
   350	                )
   351	
   352	    return errors, warnings
   353	
   354	
   355	def _append_universe_row(row, universe_csv_path=CSV_PATH):
   356	    """Append a fully-formed row dict to the coverage universe CSV.
   357	
   358	    Mirrors `universe.watchlist._append_universe_row` for new-ticker creation
   359	    via `add(..., create_if_missing=True)`.
   360	    """
   361	    path = Path(universe_csv_path)
   362	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
   363	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
   364	        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
   365	        existing_rows = list(reader)
   366	
   367	    new_row = {col: row.get(col, "") for col in fieldnames}
   368	    for col in row:
   369	        if col not in fieldnames:
   370	            fieldnames.append(col)
   371	            new_row[col] = row[col]
   372	
   373	    existing_rows.append(new_row)
   374	    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
   375	        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
   376	        writer.writeheader()
   377	        writer.writerows(existing_rows)
   378	
   379	
   380	def add(ticker, position, notes="",
   381	        first_buy_date="", average_cost=None, shares=None,
   382	        path=POSITIONS_PATH, universe_csv_path=CSV_PATH, today=None,
   383	        create_if_missing=False, sector_jp=None, exchange_hint=None,
   384	        dry_run=False):
   385	    """Add a ticker to the positions file (or update its fields if already present).
   386	
   387	    `position` must be one of "Portfolio" or "Researching" (case-sensitive).
   388	
   389	    Same new-ticker escape hatch as `universe.watchlist.add` —
   390	    `create_if_missing=True` auto-enriches a new universe row when the
   391	    ticker isn't already covered.
   392	    """
   393	    ticker = (ticker or "").strip()
   394	    if not ticker:
   395	        raise PositionsError("ticker is required")
   396	
   397	    if position not in ALLOWED_POSITION_VALUES:
   398	        raise PositionsError(
   399	            f"position must be one of {sorted(ALLOWED_POSITION_VALUES)}, "
   400	            f"got {position!r}"
   401	        )
   402	
   403	    universe_rows = _load_universe_rows(universe_csv_path)
   404	    universe_row_created = None
   405	
   406	    if ticker not in universe_rows:
   407	        if not create_if_missing:
   408	            raise PositionsError(
   409	                f"{ticker} is not in the coverage universe — add it via "
   410	                f"discovery first, or re-run with create_if_missing=True "
   411	                f"(CLI: --sector <Sector>) to auto-enrich"
   412	            )
   413	        if not sector_jp:
   414	            raise PositionsError(
   415	                f"{ticker} is not in the coverage universe and no sector_jp "
   416	                f"was provided — sector is required when creating a new "
   417	                f"universe row (it's user-curated, no API can fill it)"
   418	            )
   419	        from universe.enrich import enrich_single_ticker, EnrichError
   420	        try:
   421	            universe_row_created = enrich_single_ticker(
   422	                ticker, sector_jp=sector_jp, exchange_hint=exchange_hint
   423	            )
   424	        except EnrichError as e:
   425	            raise PositionsError(f"could not enrich {ticker}: {e}") from e
   426	
   427	    avg_cost = _parse_price(average_cost, "Average Cost") if average_cost not in (None, "") else None
   428	    n_shares = _parse_shares(shares, "Shares") if shares not in (None, "") else None
   429	
   430	    entries = load(path)
   431	    existing = next((e for e in entries if e["Ticker"] == ticker), None)
   432	    if existing:
   433	        # `position` names ONE state; setting it makes that flag true and clears
   434	        # the others. `add` has always been "put this ticker in this state", and
   435	        # keeping that meaning is what stops a caller half-migrating a row. To
   436	        # carry two states at once (a bellwether you have started underwriting),
   437	        # use `set_state`, which touches one flag and leaves the rest alone.
   438	        for _f in STATE_FLAGS:
   439	            existing[_f] = "Y" if _f == position else ""
   440	        if first_buy_date:
   441	            existing["First Buy Date"] = first_buy_date
   442	        if avg_cost is not None:
   443	            existing["Average Cost"] = avg_cost
   444	        if n_shares is not None:
   445	            existing["Shares"] = n_shares
   446	        if notes:
   447	            existing["Notes"] = notes
   448	        entry = existing
   449	    else:
   450	        entry = {
   451	            "Ticker": ticker,
   452	            "Position Date": (today or date.today().isoformat()),
   453	            "First Buy Date": first_buy_date or "",
   454	            "Average Cost": avg_cost,
   455	            "Shares": n_shares,
   456	            "Notes": notes or "",
   457	            **{_f: ("Y" if _f == position else "") for _f in STATE_FLAGS},
   458	        }
   459	        entries.append(entry)
   460	
   461	    if dry_run:
   462	        return {
   463	            "positions_entry": entry,
   464	            "universe_row": universe_row_created,
   465	            "would_create_universe_row": universe_row_created is not None,
   466	        }
   467	
   468	    if universe_row_created is not None:
   469	        _append_universe_row(universe_row_created, universe_csv_path=universe_csv_path)
   470	    save(entries, path)
   471	    return entry
   472	
   473	
   474	def set_state(ticker, flag, on=True, path=POSITIONS_PATH):
   475	    """Turn ONE intent flag on or off, leaving every other state untouched.
   476	
   477	    This is the surface a "add JPM to following for interest" instruction lands
   478	    on, and it is deliberately not `add`: `add` means *put this ticker in this
   479	    state*, which clears the others. The states genuinely co-occur -- a bellwether
   480	    you have started underwriting is both Following for Interest and Researching --
   481	    and an instruction about one of them must not silently drop the other.
   482	
   483	    Returns (entry, changed). `changed` is False when the flag already had that
   484	    value, so a caller can stay quiet rather than announcing a no-op.
   485	    """
   486	    if flag not in STATE_FLAGS:
   487	        raise PositionsError(f"unknown state {flag!r}; expected one of {STATE_FLAGS}")
   488	    ticker = ticker.strip().upper()
   489	    entries = load(path)
   490	    entry = next((e for e in entries if e["Ticker"].strip().upper() == ticker), None)
   491	    if entry is None:
   492	        raise PositionsError(
   493	            f"{ticker} is not in the positions file - add it first "
   494	            f"(it must also be in the coverage universe)"
   495	        )
   496	    want = "Y" if on else ""
   497	    if (entry.get(flag) or "") == want:
   498	        return entry, False
   499	    entry[flag] = want
   500	    save(entries, path)
   501	    return entry, True
   502	
   503	
   504	def remove(ticker, path=POSITIONS_PATH):
   505	    """Remove a ticker from the positions file. Returns True if removed, False if not found."""
   506	    ticker = (ticker or "").strip()
   507	    entries = load(path)
   508	    new_entries = [e for e in entries if e["Ticker"] != ticker]
   509	    if len(new_entries) == len(entries):
   510	        return False
   511	    save(new_entries, path)
   512	    return True

   446	def load_feed(path=None) -> HeldFeed:
   447	    """Read and VALIDATE the ownership feed. Raises `HeldFeedError` on anything
   448	    that would make acting on it a guess."""
   449	    p = Path(DEFAULT_FEED_PATH if path is None else path)
   450	    if not p.exists():
   451	        raise HeldFeedError(
   452	            f"ownership feed not found at {p} — run `python -m scripts.export_held` "
   453	            f"in portfolio_daily (it also runs at the end of the daily digest)"
   454	        )
   455	    try:
   456	        payload = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   457	    except Exception as exc:                                    # noqa: BLE001
   458	        raise HeldFeedError(f"ownership feed at {p} is unreadable: {exc}") from exc
   459	
   460	    schema = payload.get("schema")
   461	    if schema not in ACCEPTED_FEED_SCHEMAS:
   462	        raise HeldFeedError(
   463	            f"ownership feed schema {schema!r} not in accepted {sorted(ACCEPTED_FEED_SCHEMAS)} "
   464	            f"— the publisher changed shape; update this consumer deliberately"
   465	        )
   466	
   467	    age = payload.get("stalest_age_days")
   468	    if age is None:
   469	        raise HeldFeedError("ownership feed carries no stalest_age_days — cannot judge freshness")
   470	    if not _finite(age):
   471	        # `NaN > limit` is False, so a NaN age reported the feed as FRESH.
   472	        raise HeldFeedError(
   473	            f"ownership feed carries a non-finite stalest_age_days ({age!r}) — it cannot "
   474	            f"be judged fresh or stale, and comparing against it silently reports FRESH")
   475	    if float(age) > HELD_STALE_MAX_DAYS:
   476	        raise HeldFeedError(
   477	            f"ownership feed is {float(age):.1f}d old (limit {HELD_STALE_MAX_DAYS:.0f}d) — "
   478	            f"refresh the brokers first; acting on it would guess at sales"
   479	        )
   480	
   481	    raw_rows = payload.get("held") or []
   482	    if not raw_rows:
   483	        raise HeldFeedError(
   484	            "ownership feed lists zero holdings — refusing to treat an empty book as "
   485	            "'everything was sold'"
   486	        )
   487	
   488	    rows: dict[str, HeldRow] = {}
   489	    aliased: list[str] = []
   490	    merged: list[str] = []
   491	    for r in raw_rows:
   492	        t = str(r.get("ticker", "")).strip().upper()
   493	        if not t:
   494	            continue
   495	        if t in SYMBOL_ALIASES:
   496	            aliased.append(f"{t}->{SYMBOL_ALIASES[t]}")
   497	            t = SYMBOL_ALIASES[t]
   498	        if not _finite(r.get("shares") or 0.0):
   499	            raise HeldFeedError(
   500	                f"ownership feed row {t} carries a non-finite share count "
   501	                f"({r.get('shares')!r}) — every comparison against it is False, so it "
   502	                f"would DISABLE the guards below rather than trip them")
   503	        if r.get("avg_cost") is not None and not _finite(r["avg_cost"]):
   504	            raise HeldFeedError(
   505	                f"ownership feed row {t} carries a non-finite average cost "
   506	                f"({r.get('avg_cost')!r})")
   507	        shares = float(r.get("shares") or 0.0)
   508	        avg_cost = None if r.get("avg_cost") is None else float(r["avg_cost"])
   509	        # The positions book cannot HOLD these: `positions.load` rejects a negative
   510	        # share count and a non-positive cost, so writing one leaves a file every
   511	        # later sync and export refuses to read (Codex, #347 round 6 -- an auto-added
   512	        # row made it reachable for a brand-new name; any promotion or refresh could
   513	        # already do it).
   514	        #   * cost <= 0 -> UNKNOWN, not an abort. portfolio_daily publishes 0.0 for a
   515	        #     Fidelity holding with no basis at all (import_fidelity.py), so refusing
   516	        #     it would stop the whole sync every day over a real position (Codex
   517	        #     round 7: a guard becoming the outage). None is what it means.
   518	        #   * shares < 0 -> abort. The publisher never emits it (export_held skips
   519	        #     any aggregate <= 0), so it can only be a broken feed.
   520	        if avg_cost is not None and avg_cost <= 0:
   521	            logger.warning("held feed: %s carries avg_cost=%r - recorded as unknown "
   522	                           "basis (the positions book cannot hold a non-positive cost)",
   523	                           t, avg_cost)
   524	            avg_cost = None
   525	        if shares < 0:
   526	            raise HeldFeedError(
   527	                f"ownership feed row {t} carries shares={shares!r} - the positions book "
   528	                f"rejects a negative share count, so writing it would leave a file "
   529	                f"nothing can read. Fix the publisher; nothing has been written")
   530	        brokers = list(r.get("brokers") or [])
   531	        prior = rows.get(t)
   532	        if prior is None:
   533	            rows[t] = HeldRow(ticker=t, shares=shares, avg_cost=avg_cost, brokers=brokers)
   534	            continue
   535	        # TWO FEED ROWS CAN NORMALIZE ONTO ONE TICKER, AND ASSIGNING WOULD EAT ONE.
   536	        # The same issuer held at two brokers under two spellings (Fidelity `FI`,
   537	        # IBKR `FISV`) arrives as two rows; `rows[t] = ...` kept whichever came
   538	        # last, silently dropping the other broker's shares and cost basis, and
   539	        # the survivor's broker list then understated where the position is held.
   540	        # Merge instead: shares add, brokers union, and the cost basis is
   541	        # SHARE-WEIGHTED because two lots at different prices have one blended
   542	        # basis and picking either lot's price would misstate P&L on both.
   543	        total = prior.shares + shares
   544	        if prior.avg_cost is None or avg_cost is None:
   545	            # A blend needs both sides. One missing basis makes the blend
   546	            # unknowable, and inventing it from the half we have is worse than
   547	            # admitting we do not know it.
   548	            merged_cost = None
   549	        elif total > 0:
   550	            merged_cost = (prior.avg_cost * prior.shares + avg_cost * shares) / total
   551	        else:
   552	            merged_cost = None
   553	        rows[t] = HeldRow(
   554	            ticker=t,
   555	            shares=total,
   556	            avg_cost=merged_cost,
   557	            brokers=sorted(set(prior.brokers) | set(brokers)),
   558	        )
   559	        merged.append(t)
   560	
   561	    # ⛑ THE EMPTY-FEED GUARD CHECKED THE RAW LIST, NOT WHAT SURVIVED PARSING.
   562	    #
   563	    # Rows with a blank ticker are skipped above, so a feed of `[{"ticker": "",
   564	    # ...}]` is non-empty going in and empty coming out — it sails past the
   565	    # "refusing to treat an empty book as everything-was-sold" check and marks the
   566	    # WHOLE book sold, with two demotions comfortably under the circuit breaker
   567	    # (Codex round 4). One blank row among good ones fabricates one sale the same
   568	    # way. The guard has to be applied to the rows that will actually be compared.
   569	    skipped = len(raw_rows) - len(rows) - len(merged)
   570	    if not rows:
   571	        raise HeldFeedError(
   572	            f"ownership feed carried {len(raw_rows)} row(s) but none had a usable "
   573	            f"ticker — refusing to treat that as 'everything was sold'")
   574	    if skipped > 0:
   575	        raise HeldFeedError(
   576	            f"ownership feed has {skipped} row(s) with no ticker among {len(raw_rows)} "
   577	            f"— each one is a holding this sync cannot see, and an unseen holding "
   578	            f"reads as a sale. Fix the publisher; nothing has been written")
   579	
   580	    feed = HeldFeed(
   581	        schema=int(schema),
   582	        generated_at=str(payload.get("generated_at", "")),
   583	        stalest_age_days=float(age),
   584	        rows=rows,
   585	    )
   586	    feed._broker_dates = [str(b.get("as_of") or "") for b in (payload.get("brokers") or [])]
   587	    feed.aliased = aliased
   588	    if merged:
   589	        logger.warning("held feed: %s arrived under more than one symbol and were "
   590	                       "MERGED (shares summed, brokers unioned, cost basis "
   591	                       "share-weighted): %s", len(set(merged)), ", ".join(sorted(set(merged))))
   592	    if aliased:
   593	        # Never silent: an alias is a claim that two symbols are one company, and a
   594	        # wrong one would merge two issuers' holdings without a trace.
   595	        logger.warning("held feed symbol alias applied: %s (see SYMBOL_ALIASES / board #345)",
   596	                       ", ".join(aliased))
   597	    return feed

   602	
   603	def migrate_legacy_portfolio(entries, feed: "HeldFeed"):
   604	    """One-time: move rows still carrying the retired `Position == "Portfolio"`.
   605	
   606	    Returns `(new_entries, migrated_tickers)`. Idempotent by construction -- after
   607	    the first run no row can hold that value, because it is no longer in
   608	    `ALLOWED_POSITION_VALUES`, so this is inert on every subsequent call. Folded
   609	    into `sync-held` rather than given its own command so there is nothing for a
   610	    human to remember to run first, and nothing that half-migrates if they forget.
   611	
   612	    They land on `Researching`, which is the same place a SALE lands a name. That
   613	    is deliberate and makes the sale path almost a no-op on this column: a held
   614	    name's intent is already the state it will occupy once it is sold, so selling
   615	    it changes the FACT (`Held`) without disturbing the JUDGEMENT. `researching.json`
   616	    still excludes held names (see weekly_universe), so nothing appears in two
   617	    exported lists at once and no consumer sees a membership change from this.
   618	
   619	    ## A legacy `Portfolio` row absent from the feed was ALREADY sold
   620	
   621	    On the first run nothing carries `Held == "Y"` yet, so `plan_sync` cannot see a
   622	    demotion -- those rows would simply fail to be promoted and land on `Held = "N"`
   623	    looking as though they had never been owned. That would lose the history for
   624	    exactly the three names that motivated this work (ROIV, RPD, U). So the
   625	    migration marks them `Previously Held` here, where the old value still carries
   626	    the evidence: `Position == "Portfolio"` MEANT held, so a legacy row missing from
   627	    the broker feed is a sale that already happened.
   628	
   629	    `Held Until` is deliberately left EMPTY for them. We know the name is gone by the
   630	    feed's as-of; we do not know the day it sold -- ROIV was 2026-08-03 and RPD/U
   631	    2026-08-21, and the feed cannot distinguish them. Stamping the as-of would write
   632	    a sale date that every downstream reader would take as fact. They are returned by
   633	    name instead, so the operator can fill the real dates if they matter.
   634	    """
   635	    from universe import positions as _pos
   636	
   637	    migrated = []
   638	    already_sold = []
   639	    out = []
   640	    for e in entries:
   641	        e = dict(e)
   642	        # Keyed on the FLAGS being empty, never on `Position`. Since 2026-08-23
   643	        # `Position` is a DERIVED MIRROR that `save()` recomputes -- and it prints
   644	        # "Portfolio" for every held row -- so a Position-keyed check re-fires on
   645	        # all 30 holdings every single run and reports a migration it did not do.
   646	        # The genuine legacy shape is a row with no intent flag at all; `load()`
   647	        # upgrades anything that still has the old column, so in practice this is
   648	        # now inert, which is exactly what a completed migration should be.
   649	        is_legacy = (
   650	            not any(_pos.has_state(e, f) for f in _pos.STATE_FLAGS)
   651	            and not _pos.is_held(e)
   652	            and (e.get("Position") or "").strip() == LEGACY_POSITION
   653	        )
   654	        if is_legacy:
   655	            ticker = e["Ticker"].strip().upper()
   656	            e[DEMOTION_POSITION] = "Y"
   657	            migrated.append(ticker)
   658	            if ticker not in feed.rows:
   659	                e["Previously Held"] = "Y"
   660	                e["Held"] = "N"
   661	                e["Held Until"] = ""      # unknown on purpose -- see docstring
   662	                already_sold.append(ticker)
   663	        out.append(e)
   664	    return out, sorted(migrated), sorted(already_sold)
   665

   667	def plan_sync(entries, feed: HeldFeed, universe_tickers=None, accept_partial_join: bool = False,
   668	              metadata_incomplete=None) -> SyncPlan:
   669	    """Compute the change WITHOUT touching disk.
   670	
   671	    `entries` is `positions.load()` output. Pure function so the dry-run and the
   672	    real run cannot disagree about what is about to happen.
   673	
   674	    `metadata_incomplete` names universe tickers whose row lacks a field
   675	    `positions.validate` requires. Such a name is never AUTO-ADDED: the row would
   676	    fail positions validation, and `catalyst_watch` gates the WHOLE positions export
   677	    on `validation_passed` -- one incomplete auto-added row would drop every name
   678	    from that lane. It is reported in `held_without_row` instead (Codex, #347 r2).
   679	    """
   680	    plan = SyncPlan(feed_as_of=feed.as_of)
   681	    by_ticker = {e["Ticker"].strip().upper(): e for e in entries}
   682	
   683	    if universe_tickers is not None:
   684	        known = {t.strip().upper() for t in universe_tickers}
   685	        plan.not_in_universe = sorted(t for t in feed.rows if t not in known)
   686	        # ⛑ The gap between the two checks (board #347). `not_in_universe` asks "is the
   687	        # broker holding a name CM does not cover?"; the loop below asks "did any
   688	        # EXISTING row change?". A freshly bought name that IS covered answers no to
   689	        # both, so it was dropped from `Held` on a green run with every counter empty.
   690	        # The module's own docstring claimed a held ticker was "reported every run and
   691	        # never silently dropped"; this is the case that claim missed.
   692	        rowless = sorted(t for t in feed.rows if t in known and t not in by_ticker)
   693	        incomplete = {t.strip().upper() for t in (metadata_incomplete or ())}
   694	        unfit = [t for t in rowless if t in incomplete]
   695	        rowless = [t for t in rowless if t not in incomplete]
   696	        # JP 2026-09-26: "once you see it's in my portfolio shouldn't you just update
   697	        # it automatically" -> "yes". So these are CREATED, not merely named -- unless
   698	        # there are more than a real week of purchases, in which case none are.
   699	        # The cap counts EVERY covered rowless name, creatable or not: it is a signal
   700	        # about the FEED, and an incomplete universe row does not make a dozen new
   701	        # names any likelier to be real (Codex, #347 round 5).
   702	        if len(rowless) + len(unfit) > MAX_AUTO_ADDS_PER_RUN:
   703	            plan.held_without_row = sorted(rowless + unfit)
   704	        else:
   705	            plan.held_without_row = unfit
   706	            # The universe's own spelling, so the created row joins its universe row
   707	            # exactly (`positions.validate` matches tickers verbatim). On a case-only
   708	            # universe duplicate the upper-case spelling wins, else the first sorted.
   709	            spellings: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   710	            for raw in universe_tickers:
   711	                spellings.setdefault(raw.strip().upper(), []).append(raw.strip())
   712	            plan.auto_added = [
   713	                t if t in spellings[t] else sorted(spellings[t])[0] for t in rowless]
   714	
   715	    for ticker, entry in sorted(by_ticker.items()):
   716	        was_held = (entry.get("Held") or "").strip().upper() == "Y"
   717	        now_held = ticker in feed.rows
   718	        if now_held and not was_held:
   719	            plan.promotions.append(ticker)
   720	        elif was_held and not now_held:
   721	            plan.demotions.append(ticker)
   722	        elif now_held and was_held:
   723	            plan.refreshed.append(ticker)
   724	
   725	    # ⛑ AN UNJOINED FEED ROW ALONGSIDE A DEMOTION IS THE FALSE-SALE SIGNATURE.
   726	    #
   727	    # This guard is at the point of HARM, and that is the whole point: it does not
   728	    # care WHY a symbol failed to join. Codex round 2 showed the alias-store
   729	    # guards could not cover the case — `_load_symbol_aliases` raises on an
   730	    # UNREADABLE store, but a MISSING one legitimately yields an empty map, and a
   731	    # store whose entry contradicts the universe is never checked here at all
   732	    # (`held.py` reads `data/ticker_aliases.json` directly, so the publish-side
   733	    # guard is irrelevant to it). Both roads lead here: the feed's `FISV` does not
   734	    # join the universe's `FI`, `FI` is planned as a demotion, one demotion is far
   735	    # under MAX_DEMOTIONS_PER_RUN, and a real position is written out as sold.
   736	    #
   737	    # `not_in_universe` is only populated when the caller passes `universe_tickers`
   738	    # — without it we cannot see the signature and do not pretend to.
   739	    # ⛑ THE MATCH IS ON SHARE COUNT, NOT ON CO-OCCURRENCE.
   740	    #
   741	    # v1 of this guard blocked whenever ANY demotion coincided with ANY unjoined
   742	    # feed holding, which is the shape of a fabricated sale and also the shape of
   743	    # an ordinary week: sell a covered name, buy an uncovered one, and the whole
   744	    # sync aborted while the sold name kept publishing as owned (Codex round 3).
   745	    # That is "a guard can become the outage", and it contradicted this module's
   746	    # own documented contract that an uncovered holding is NOT fatal.
   747	    #
   748	    # The discriminator is cheap and strong: a fabricated sale is ONE position
   749	    # seen twice, so the unjoined feed row carries the SAME share count the
   750	    # position record already holds. A genuine rebalance has no such coincidence.
   751	    # A demoted row with no recorded share count cannot be matched either way, so
   752	    # it is reported and allowed through rather than blocking on ignorance.
   753	    # ⛑ THE RULE IS "SHARES LOST == SHARES UNJOINED", AND A DEMOTION IS ONLY ITS
   754	    #    EXTREME CASE. v1 of this guard looked at demotions alone, so a PARTIAL
   755	    #    split slipped through untouched: a 30-share position held at two brokers
   756	    #    under two spellings, with the alias store gone, arrives as `FI: 10` plus
   757	    #    an unjoined `FISV: 20`. That is `refreshed`, not a demotion — unblocked,
   758	    #    and `apply_plan` overwrote 30 shares with 10 and one broker's cost basis
   759	    #    with the other's (Codex round 4). Same defect, two thirds of the way
   760	    #    along. Generalising to "recorded minus new" covers both, and a demotion
   760	    #    along. Generalising to "recorded minus new" covers both, and a demotion
   761	    #    falls out as new == 0.
   762	    # ⛑ RUN THE ALIAS STORE'S OWN VALIDATOR, DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT ONE OF ITS RULES.
   763	    #
   764	    # Four adversarial rounds over this feature found three separate roads to a
   765	    # wrong ownership record, and all three were the SAME structural fault: a
   766	    # check that existed on the PUBLISH side and not on the read side, because
   767	    # this module reads `data/ticker_aliases.json` directly and the export
   768	    # pipeline never runs for it.
   769	    #
   770	    # The first fix here was a hand-rolled version of `check_universe`'s fatal
   771	    # rule (an alias that is also a covered row — resolve through it and two
   772	    # separately-covered companies merge into one holding). That closed the
   773	    # instance and left the class open: a hand copy of one of three rules drifts
   774	    # from the original the first time the original changes. Calling the real
   775	    # validator closes all three and cannot drift.
   776	    #
   777	    # A ticker list is all this function is given, so only the rules that key on
   778	    # tickers can fire; the identity-anchor rule needs columns we do not have and
   779	    # skips itself on blanks, which is its documented behaviour, not a silent hole.
   780	    # ⛑ VALIDATE THE MAP THAT WAS ACTUALLY APPLIED, AND NEVER DISCARD A HAZARD.
   781	    #
   782	    # Two defects lived in the first version of this block, both found by review:
   783	    #
   784	    #   * it RELOADED the store from disk while `load_feed` had already normalised
   785	    #     the feed with the import-time `SYMBOL_ALIASES`. Change the file in
   786	    #     between — Dropbox sync, a concurrent edit — and it validated bytes that
   787	    #     never touched the data, which is "the reviewed thing is not the
   788	    #     published thing" with a validator playing the reviewer;
   789	    #   * its `except` set `problems = []`, so a hazard `merge_hazards` had
   790	    #     ALREADY confirmed was erased when the advisory call raised afterwards.
   791	    #     A fatal, once found, is never unfound.
   792	    #
   793	    # The advisory `check_universe` pass was also dropped rather than kept. It was
   794	    # handed a frame carrying only `Ticker`, so its CIK/ISIN/FIGI rules skip on
   795	    # blanks every single time — a three-rule validator of which one rule could
   796	    # ever fire, logging as though all three had. A check that cannot match is
   797	    # worse than no check, because it reads like coverage.
   798	    if universe_tickers:
   799	        # The store's OWN rule, applied to the exact map `load_feed` used. Not a
   800	        # fresh read (which would validate bytes that never touched the data) and
   801	        # not a hand copy (which would drift from the original). Both were live
   802	        # defects here before this line.
   803	        try:
   804	            from universe.aliases import merge_hazards_for_map
   805	
   806	            hazards = merge_hazards_for_map(SYMBOL_ALIASES, universe_tickers)
   807	        except ImportError:
   808	            hazards = []
   809	        if hazards:
   810	            plan.blocked_reason = (
   811	                "the alias map applied to this feed would resolve a covered company "
   812	                "onto another: " + "; ".join(hazards[:4])
   813	                + (f" ... +{len(hazards) - 4} more" if len(hazards) > 4 else "")
   814	                + ". Fix data/ticker_aliases.json or the universe row, then re-run."
   815	            )
   816	            return plan
   817	
   818	    # ⛑ A DEMOTION IS THE ONLY DESTRUCTIVE OPERATION HERE, SO IT IS THE ONLY ONE
   819	    #    WITHHELD WHEN THE JOIN CANNOT BE TRUSTED.
   820	    #
   821	    # This replaces a share-count heuristic that matched "shares lost == shares
   822	    # unjoined" and blocked the whole run on a hit. Fable disproved its premise:
   823	    # **a symbol change and a share-count change CO-OCCUR at a corporate action**,
   824	    # which is precisely the moment no alias entry exists yet. Reproduced against
   825	    # these files -- a 3-share DRIP (100 -> 103) made the numbers unequal, the
   826	    # match missed, and a fabricated sale of the real position was WRITTEN:
   827	    # Held=N, Shares cleared, Held Until stamped. Splits, conversions and an added
   828	    # buy all do the same. A guard whose premise fails exactly when it is needed
   829	    # is not a guard.
   830	    #
   831	    # The replacement asserts nothing about identity. It says only: while some
   832	    # feed holding did not join, or while a promotion looks like the other half of
   833	    # a demotion, WE CANNOT TELL a sale from a re-spelling -- so promotions and
   834	    # refreshes still apply and the demotions are held back and named. That is
   835	    # strictly safer than the heuristic (it cannot fabricate a sale at all) and
   836	    # strictly cheaper than the round-3 version (it does not block the run, so an
   837	    # uncovered holding never stops an ordinary rebalance). The cost is a `Held`
   838	    # that stays stale for a run, reported every time and exiting non-zero -- the
   839	    # trade this module's own docstring already makes: never read absence as sold.
   840	    withhold_reasons = []
   841	    # A feed holding with no row that this run does NOT create (`held_without_row`:
   842	    # over the auto-add cap, or an incomplete universe row) did not join the book
   843	    # either, so it is exactly as able to be the other half of a rename or a split as
   844	    # an uncovered one. Before #347's auto-add these names were ignored here and a
   845	    # covered rename OLD -> NEW stamped OLD sold (Codex, #347 round 3).
   846	    unjoined = plan.not_in_universe + plan.held_without_row
   847	    if plan.demotions and unjoined:
   848	        withhold_reasons.append(
   849	            f"{len(unjoined)} feed holding(s) did not join the "
   850	            f"{'positions book' if plan.held_without_row else 'universe'} "
   851	            f"({', '.join(unjoined[:5])})")
   852	
   853	    # The same doubt without any unjoined row: a promotion carrying a demotion's
   854	    # share count is the shape of ONE position moving between two covered rows --
   855	    # the case where the universe holds two rows for one issuer and no alias links
   856	    # them. Zero unjoined holdings, so the check above cannot see it.
   857	    #
   858	    # An AUTO-ADDED row is a promotion for this purpose (board #347, 2026-09-26): it
   859	    # is a covered name joining Held, which is exactly the other half of a rename.
   860	    # Before auto-add such a name was not promoted at all, so this check could not
   861	    # see it; now that it IS written as held, leaving it out would let a covered
   862	    # rename OLD -> NEW stamp OLD sold while NEW is created beside it.
   863	    joined = plan.promotions + [t.upper() for t in plan.auto_added]
   864	    if plan.demotions and joined:
   865	        # NO SHARE COMPARISON HERE. The previous version required the promoted row
   866	        # to carry the SAME count as the demoted one -- the exact premise this
   867	        # redesign was written to delete, left gating the covered-row path. Codex
   868	        # round 6: a corporate action producing covered NEW at 103 against OLD at
   869	        # 100 slipped straight through and OLD was stamped sold, because the
   870	        # counts differ at precisely the event that renames a symbol.
   871	        #
   872	        # Without an identity anchor we genuinely cannot tell "sold X, bought Y"
   873	        # from "X became Y", so we do not pretend to: any demotion coinciding with
   874	        # any promotion is deferred. That over-defers a real rotation week by one
   875	        # run, which is why `--accept-partial-join` exists as the release.
   876	        withhold_reasons.append(
   877	            f"{len(joined)} name(s) joined Held in the same run "
   878	            f"({', '.join(joined[:5])}) -- with no identity anchor on the "
   879	            f"feed, a rename is indistinguishable from a sale plus a purchase")
   880	
   881	    # A REFRESH CAN LOSE SHARES TO AN UNJOINED SYMBOL TOO, and that is corruption
   882	    # rather than a fabricated sale: the position survives with the WRONG count.
   883	    # 30 shares held across two brokers under two spellings arrive as FI:10 plus an
   884	    # unjoined FISV:20, and writing 10 silently discards two thirds of the holding
   885	    # and one broker's cost basis. Same doubt, same answer -- hold the figures back
   886	    # rather than write a number we cannot trust.
   887	    if unjoined:
   888	        for ticker in list(plan.refreshed):
   889	            recorded = _shares_of(by_ticker.get(ticker, {}))
   890	            now = feed.rows[ticker].shares if ticker in feed.rows else None
   891	            if recorded is None or now is None or not _finite(now):
   892	                continue
   893	            # ANY difference, not just a decrease. Requiring `recorded > now` kept
   894	            # the same share-direction assumption the redesign rejects: with a
   895	            # joined leg at 35 against a stored 30 and an unjoined 20, the refresh
   896	            # was allowed and wrote 35, discarding 20 shares and their basis
   897	            # (Codex round 6). An unjoined holding could belong to ANY covered row,
   898	            # so any figure that moves while one exists is a figure we cannot trust.
   899	            if abs(recorded - now) > SHARE_MATCH_TOLERANCE:
   900	                plan.refreshed.remove(ticker)
   901	                plan.withheld_refreshes.append(ticker)
   902	                withhold_reasons.append(
   903	                    f"{ticker} would drop {recorded - now:g} share(s) while "
   904	                    f"{len(unjoined)} holding(s) did not join")
   905	
   906	    # ⛑ THE RELEASE. Without one, a single persistently-uncovered holding defers
   907	    # every real sale FOREVER, and exit 2 is a repeated warning, not a mechanism --
   908	    # which recreates the exact stale-held failure this module exists to prevent
   909	    # (ROIV published as held for 19 days). Codex round 6. The operator who has
   910	    # looked at the named holdings and decided they are unrelated passes
   911	    # `--accept-partial-join`; the reasons are still printed, so the decision is
   912	    # recorded in the run output rather than made silently by a default.
   913	    if withhold_reasons and accept_partial_join:
   914	        # The refreshes withheld above go BACK into `refreshed`: the release said it
   915	        # applied "figure updates", but they stayed in `withheld_refreshes`, which
   916	        # `apply_plan` skips and the CLI exits 2 on -- so the release could never
   917	        # release them and the stale count stood for ever (Codex, #347 round 4;
   918	        # pre-existing, made reachable by more names counting as unjoined).
   919	        plan.refreshed = sorted(plan.refreshed + plan.withheld_refreshes)
   920	        plan.withheld_refreshes = []
   921	        logger.warning(
   922	            "accept-partial-join: applying %d demotion(s) and %d figure update(s) "
   923	            "the join could not vouch for, on operator instruction: %s",
   924	            len(plan.demotions), len(plan.refreshed), "; ".join(withhold_reasons))
   925	        plan.accepted_partial_join = True
   926	        withhold_reasons = []
   927	
   928	    if withhold_reasons:
   929	        plan.withheld_demotions = list(plan.demotions)
   930	        plan.demotions = []
   931	        plan.withheld_reason = (
   932	            f"{len(plan.withheld_demotions)} demotion(s) and "
   933	            f"{len(plan.withheld_refreshes)} figure update(s) WITHHELD "
   934	            f"({', '.join(plan.withheld_demotions)}) because the join cannot be "
   935	            f"trusted this run: " + "; ".join(withhold_reasons)
   936	            + ". Everything else was applied. Nothing was marked sold and no figure was "
   937	            "overwritten with a number that could not be trusted -- "
   938	            "a sale that is real will apply on the next run once the holding is "
   939	            "covered or its symbols are recorded in data/ticker_aliases.json."
   940	        )
   941	        logger.warning("%s", plan.withheld_reason)
   942	
   943	    # ⛑ COUNT THE WITHHELD DEMOTIONS TOO. The withhold above empties
   944	    # `plan.demotions`, so a breaker counting only what is left never fires on the
   945	    # exact feed it exists for: a fresh, well-formed, WRONG feed carrying one covered
   946	    # name and none of the 30 real holdings withheld all 30 and then wrote the one
   947	    # (Codex, board #347 round 2 -- auto-add made the promotion that triggers the
   948	    # withhold out of a rowless name, but a promoted or uncovered one did it before).
   949	    # A name the feed says left Held is a name leaving Held for this test, whether
   950	    # this run applies the sale or defers it.
   951	    leaving = plan.demotions + plan.withheld_demotions
   952	    if len(leaving) > MAX_DEMOTIONS_PER_RUN:
   953	        plan.blocked_reason = (
   954	            f"{len(leaving)} names would leave Held in one run "
   955	            f"(limit {MAX_DEMOTIONS_PER_RUN}): {', '.join(sorted(leaving))}. "
   956	            f"That is more than a rebalance — check the publisher before overriding."
   957	        )
   958	    return plan
   959

   961	def apply_plan(entries, feed: HeldFeed, plan: SyncPlan, today=None):
   962	    """Return NEW entries with the derived columns written. Never mutates input.
   963	
   964	    Raises if the plan is blocked — a blocked plan must not reach disk by any path.
   965	    """
   966	    if plan.is_blocked:
   967	        raise HeldFeedError(f"refusing to apply a blocked plan: {plan.blocked_reason}")
   968	
   969	    stamp = (today or date.today()).isoformat()
   970	
   971	    # Board #347 (JP 2026-09-26): create the row for a covered holding that had none,
   972	    # then let the loop below promote it exactly as it promotes any other row -- one
   973	    # promotion path, so an auto-added row cannot end up in a shape an ordinary
   974	    # promotion would not produce. No intent flag: every held row in the book carries
   975	    # none, because ownership is the `Held` fact, not an intent (`positions.add`
   976	    # would force one, and `Portfolio` is not an intent it accepts). A ticker already
   977	    # present is never duplicated -- `plan_sync` only lists names with no row, and
   978	    # this re-checks so a stale plan cannot mint a second row.
   979	    present = {e["Ticker"].strip().upper() for e in entries}
   980	    created = []
   981	    for ticker in plan.auto_added:
   982	        if ticker.strip().upper() in present:
   983	            continue
   984	        brokers = feed.rows[ticker.strip().upper()].brokers
   985	        created.append({
   986	            "Ticker": ticker,
   987	            "Position Date": stamp,
   988	            "First Buy Date": "",
   989	            "Average Cost": None,
   990	            "Shares": None,
   991	            "Notes": (f"auto-added by sync-held {stamp}: held at "
   992	                      f"{', '.join(brokers) or 'a broker'}, no positions row existed"),
   993	            "Held": "",
   994	            "Held As Of": "",
   995	            "Previously Held": "",
   996	            "Held Until": "",
   997	            **{f: "" for f in STATE_FLAGS_FOR_DEMOTION},
   998	        })
   999	        present.add(ticker.strip().upper())
  1000	
  1001	    out = []
  1002	    for e in list(entries) + created:
  1003	        e = dict(e)
  1004	        ticker = e["Ticker"].strip().upper()
  1005	        if ticker in plan.withheld_refreshes or ticker in plan.withheld_demotions:
  1006	            # UNTOUCHED -- and this covers BOTH withheld sets, which the first
  1007	            # version did not. A withheld demotion has no feed row and was removed

  1010	            # stayed Held=Y with blank figures. I fixed this exact erasure for

  1012	            # commit, while its message claimed "a withheld row is left

  1014	            out.append(e)

  1016	        row = feed.rows.get(ticker)

  1018	            e["Held"] = "Y"
  1019	            e["Held As Of"] = plan.feed_as_of
  1020	            e["Shares"] = row.shares
  1021	            e["Average Cost"] = row.avg_cost
  1022	            e["Held Until"] = ""
  1023	        elif ticker in plan.demotions:

  1025	            # stays in every lane that reads portfolio.json + researching.json; the
  1026	            # fact that it was owned is preserved beside it rather than in Position.
  1027	            e["Held"] = "N"
  1028	            e["Held As Of"] = plan.feed_as_of

  1030	            e["Held Until"] = stamp
  1031	            # Set the FLAG. Writing `Position` alone is a dead write that `save()`
  1032	            # recomputes from the flags -- precisely what made the legacy migration
  1033	            # look like it was working when it was not.
  1034	            for _f in STATE_FLAGS_FOR_DEMOTION:

  1036	            e["Shares"] = None
  1037	            e["Average Cost"] = None
  1038	        else:
  1039	            # Not held, by any route. Share count and average cost are facts about a
  1040	            # HOLDING, so a row that is not held must not carry them -- ROIV kept
  1041	            # "3400 shares @ $5.00" from its hand-entered days after the account was
  1042	            # liquidated, which is exactly the shape of stale figure a consumer reads
  1043	            # as current. Stated as an invariant here rather than only on the
  1044	            # demotion path, so it self-heals whatever wrote them.
  1045	            e["Held"] = e.get("Held") or "N"
  1046	            e["Shares"] = None
  1047	            e["Average Cost"] = None
  1048	        out.append(e)
  1049	    return out

     1	"""Apply JP's `add` / `decline` replies in #ipo-spinoffs-newissues to the ledger.
     2	
     3	**Why this exists.** Every weekly report has ended with *"To act, reply in this
     4	thread: `add MU`, `decline MU`, or `add all`"* — and nothing read that thread.
     5	`approve_candidates.py`'s own docstring said so: *"The Slack reply-poller will call
     6	exactly this; today it is driven by hand."* The result on 2026-07-31 was three
     7	recommendations sitting `pending` with an instruction that could not work. The
     8	sibling lane (`watchlist_harmonizer`) has had `WatchlistHarmonizerReplies` polling
     9	#coverage three times a day since 2026-07-14; this is the same shape for this lane.
    10	
    11	Design rules, each earned elsewhere in the fleet:
    12	
    13	- **Gated to the pending ledger.** A reply naming a ticker that is not `pending`
    14	  is reported, never acted on. The poller can only ever resolve a decision the
    15	  report actually asked for.
    16	- **Idempotent by message timestamp**, not by outcome. A processed `ts` is
    17	  recorded whether it succeeded or failed, so a transient enrichment failure does
    18	  not re-fire the approval on the next pass — position is never the key.
    19	- **Only the approver.** Messages from anyone else, and from the bot itself, are
    20	  ignored; otherwise the bot's own "3 pending: MU" summary reads as an instruction.
    21	- **Republish, or the approval is invisible.** Writing the universe CSV changes
    22	  nothing outside this repo until `exports/` regenerates. That runs here, and its
    23	  outcome is reported — an approval that silently fails to reach the seven
    24	  downstream consumers is the same class of failure as the report nobody saw.
    25	- **Answer in the thread.** JP gets a reply saying what landed and what did not,
    26	  so a decision never disappears into a state file.
    27	
    28	Usage:
    29	    python scripts/poll_ipo_replies.py                # apply + republish
    30	    python scripts/poll_ipo_replies.py --dry-run      # parse and report only
    31	    python scripts/poll_ipo_replies.py --no-publish   # apply, skip the republish
    32	    python scripts/poll_ipo_replies.py --since 2026-08-01   # re-scan from a date

    57	# The grammar has to survive how a person actually types, not how the help text
    58	# reads. JP replied "Add all 3" on 2026-08-06; the original `^add all$` anchor

    61	VERBS = r"add|approve|decline|reject|skip"

    63	ADD_ALL = re.compile(rf"^\s*(?:add|approve)\s+all\b.*$", re.I)

    76	def _env(name: str, default: str = "") -> str:

    90	def _api(method: str, params: dict, token: str, *, post: bool = False) -> dict:
    91	    if post:
    92	        req = urllib.request.Request(
    93	            SLACK_API + method, data=json.dumps(params).encode("utf-8"),
    94	            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + token,
    95	                     "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"})
    96	    else:
    97	        req = urllib.request.Request(
    98	            SLACK_API + method + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
    99	            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + token})
   100	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
   101	        body = json.loads(resp.read())
   102	    if not body.get("ok"):
   103	        raise PollError(f"{method} failed: {body.get('error')}")
   104	    return body

   107	def load_state() -> dict:
   108	    if STATE_PATH.exists():
   109	        try:
   110	            data = json.loads(STATE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   111	            if isinstance(data, dict):

   114	        except (ValueError, OSError):
   115	            # A corrupt state file must not silently re-apply every past reply.
   116	            raise PollError(f"unreadable state file: {STATE_PATH}")
   117	    return {"applied_ts": [], "last_scan": ""}

   120	def save_state(state: dict) -> None:
   121	    state["applied_ts"] = sorted(set(state["applied_ts"]))[-500:]
   122	    state["last_scan"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
   123	    STATE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   124	    tmp = STATE_PATH.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
   125	    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
   126	    tmp.replace(STATE_PATH)

   129	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- parsing

   131	
   132	def first_line(text: str) -> str:
   133	    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
   134	        s = line.strip()
   135	        if s and not s.startswith(">"):
   136	            return s
   137	    return ""

   140	def parse_reply(text: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]] | None:
   141	    """-> (action, [TICKER, ...]) or (action, ['ALL']); None if not a command.
   142	
   143	    Returns None only for text that does not even *attempt* a command. A message
   144	    that starts with a command verb but does not parse is a different thing —
   145	    see `looks_like_command`, which is what stops an unparsed instruction from
   146	    reading as silence.
   147	    """
   148	    line = first_line(text)
   149	    if not line:
   150	        return None
   151	    # Strip Slack's leading @-mention so "@ClaudeBot add MU" works.
   152	    line = re.sub(r"^<@[A-Z0-9]+>\s*", "", line).strip()
   153	    if ADD_ALL.match(line):
   154	        return ("approve", ["ALL"])
   155	    m = DECIDE.match(line)
   156	    if not m:
   157	        return None
   158	    verb = m.group(1).lower()
   159	    # "add MU, APMD and CXMT." -> three tickers. Trailing punctuation is
   160	    # stripped per token; no ticker ends in a dot or comma.
   161	    raw = re.split(r"[,\s]+|\band\b", m.group(2), flags=re.I)
   162	    tickers = []
   163	    for tok in raw:
   164	        tok = tok.strip().strip(".,;:!?").upper()
   165	        if tok and TICKER.match(tok):
   166	            tickers.append(tok)
   167	    if not tickers:
   168	        return None
   169	    action = "approve" if verb in APPROVE_WORDS else "decline"
   170	    return (action, list(dict.fromkeys(tickers)))
   171	
   172	
   173	def looks_like_command(text: str) -> bool:
   174	    """True when the message opens with a command verb, parseable or not.
   175	
   176	    An approver message that tries to be an instruction and fails to parse must
   177	    be reported, never skipped. "Add all 3" was the live case: it reached no
   178	    branch and the run printed "no command replies found", which is exactly what
   179	    a run with no reply at all prints.
   180	    """
   181	    line = re.sub(r"^<@[A-Z0-9]+>\s*", "", first_line(text)).strip()
   182	    return bool(ATTEMPT.match(line))

   185	def collect_replies(token: str, channel: str, approver: str,
   186	                    oldest: str = "") -> list[dict]:
   187	    """Every approver message in the channel, top-level and in threads."""
   188	    params = {"channel": channel, "limit": HISTORY_LIMIT}
   189	    if oldest:
   190	        params["oldest"] = oldest
   191	    history = _api("conversations.history", params, token).get("messages", [])
   192	
   193	    found: list[dict] = []
   194	    seen_threads: set[str] = set()
   195	    for msg in history:
   196	        # JP replies at top level as often as in-thread; the harmonizer poller
   197	        # reads both for exactly this reason.
   198	        if msg.get("user") == approver and msg.get("text"):
   199	            found.append({"ts": msg["ts"], "text": msg["text"],
   200	                          "thread_ts": msg.get("thread_ts") or msg["ts"]})
   201	        parent = msg.get("thread_ts") or msg["ts"]
   202	        if msg.get("reply_count") and parent not in seen_threads:
   203	            seen_threads.add(parent)
   204	            replies = _api("conversations.replies",
   205	                           {"channel": channel, "ts": parent, "limit": 200},
   206	                           token).get("messages", [])
   207	            for r in replies:
   208	                if r.get("user") == approver and r.get("text") and r["ts"] != parent:
   209	                    found.append({"ts": r["ts"], "text": r["text"],
   210	                                  "thread_ts": parent})
   211	    # Oldest first: decisions are applied in the order JP made them.
   212	    uniq = {m["ts"]: m for m in found}
   213	    return [uniq[k] for k in sorted(uniq)]

   224	        str(row.get("subsector", "")).strip(),

   226	    ])

   232	    Runs the export + acceptance steps directly rather than shelling

   245	        _, validation = run_step("validate", wu._step_validate)
   246	        for name, fn, args in (

   248	            ("export_positions", wu._step_export_positions, ()),

   250	        ):

   255	    except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001 - report, never crash the poll
