   187	def format_price(value, currency=""):
   188	    """Format share price. USD: bare number. Foreign: currency symbol prefix."""
   189	    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
   190	        return "N/A"
   191	    v = float(value)
   192	    is_foreign = currency and currency != "USD"
   193	    prefix = _currency_prefix(currency) if is_foreign else ""
   194	    if v >= 1000:
   195	        return f"{prefix}{v:,.0f}"
   196	    return f"{prefix}{v:.2f}"
   197	
   198	
   199	# ── Return calculations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   200	
   201	def calc_annual_return(hist, year):
   202	    """Calculate total return for a calendar year.
   203	
   204	    Standard convention: measured from the PRIOR year's close (the last trading
   205	    bar before Jan 1), not the first trading bar inside the year — so the
   206	    Jan-1→first-open gap is captured. Returns None if there's no prior-year bar
   207	    to anchor on (e.g. an IPO during `year`).
   208	    """
   209	    year_data = hist[hist.index.year == year]
   210	    if year_data.empty:
   211	        return None
   212	    prior = hist[hist.index.year < year]
   213	    if prior.empty:
   214	        return None
   215	    start = prior.iloc[-1]
   216	    last = year_data.iloc[-1]
   217	    return (last / start - 1) * 100
   218	
   219	
   220	def calc_period_return(hist, days):
   221	    """Calculate return over last N calendar days from latest data point."""
   222	    if hist.empty:
   223	        return None
   224	    end = hist.iloc[-1]
   225	    target_date = hist.index[-1] - pd.Timedelta(days=days)
   226	    earlier = hist[hist.index <= target_date]
   227	    if earlier.empty:
   228	        return None
   229	    start = earlier.iloc[-1]
   230	    return (end / start - 1) * 100
   231	
   232	
   233	def calc_1d_return(hist):
   234	    """Calculate 1-day return (last close vs prior close)."""
   235	    if len(hist) < 2:
   236	        return None
   237	    return (hist.iloc[-1] / hist.iloc[-2] - 1) * 100
   238	
   239	
   240	def calc_1w_return(hist):
   241	    """Calculate 1-week return (last 5 trading days)."""
   242	    if len(hist) < 6:
   243	        return None
   244	    return (hist.iloc[-1] / hist.iloc[-6] - 1) * 100
   245	
   246	
   247	def calc_qtd_return(hist):
   248	    """Calculate quarter-to-date return.
   249	
   250	    Standard convention: measured from the PRIOR quarter's close (the last
   251	    trading bar before the quarter start), not the first bar inside the quarter.
   252	    Returns None if there's no bar before the quarter start to anchor on.
   253	    """
   254	    today = date.today()
   255	    q_start_month = ((today.month - 1) // 3) * 3 + 1
   256	    q_start = pd.Timestamp(today.year, q_start_month, 1)
   257	    qtr_data = hist[hist.index >= q_start]
   258	    if qtr_data.empty:
   259	        return None
   260	    prior = hist[hist.index < q_start]
   261	    if prior.empty:
   262	        return None
   263	    start = prior.iloc[-1]
   264	    return (qtr_data.iloc[-1] / start - 1) * 100
   265	
   266	
   267	def calc_ytd_return(hist):
   268	    """Calculate YTD return.
   269	
   270	    Standard convention: measured from the PRIOR year's close (last trading bar
   271	    before Jan 1), not the first bar inside the year. Returns None if there's no
   272	    prior-year bar to anchor on.
   273	    """
   274	    today = date.today()
   275	    year_data = hist[hist.index.year == today.year]
   276	    if year_data.empty:
   277	        return None
   278	    prior = hist[hist.index.year < today.year]
   279	    if prior.empty:
   280	        return None
   281	    start = prior.iloc[-1]
   282	    last = year_data.iloc[-1]
   283	    return (last / start - 1) * 100
   284	
   285	
   286	# ── Color formatting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   287	
   288	def get_color(value, is_negative_col=False):
   289	    """Return RGB hex color for a return value. Red for negative, green for positive, white for zero/NA."""
   290	    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
   291	        return "FFFFFF"
   292	    val = float(value)
   293	    if val == 0:
   294	        return "FFFFFF"
   295	    if val > 0:
   296	        intensity = min(abs(val) / 100, 1.0)
   297	        r = int(255 - intensity * 155)
   298	        g = int(255 - intensity * 30)
   299	        b = int(255 - intensity * 155)
   300	        return f"{r:02X}{g:02X}{b:02X}"
   301	    else:
   302	        intensity = min(abs(val) / 100, 1.0)
   303	        r = int(255 - intensity * 30)
   304	        g = int(255 - intensity * 155)
   305	        b = int(255 - intensity * 155)
   306	        return f"{r:02X}{g:02X}{b:02X}"
   307	
   308	
   309	def get_html_color(value):
   310	    """Return CSS background-color for HTML."""
   311	    hex_color = get_color(value)
   312	    return f"#{hex_color}"
   313	
   314	
   315	# ── Composite helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   316	
   317	def calc_pct_of_52wk_high(hist):
   318	    """Calculate current price as a percentage of 52-week high."""
   319	    if hist is None or len(hist) < 2:
   320	        return None
   321	    one_year_ago = hist.index[-1] - pd.Timedelta(days=365)
   322	    year_data = hist[hist.index >= one_year_ago]
   323	    if year_data.empty:
   324	        return None
   325	    high = year_data.max()
   326	    if high <= 0:
   327	        return None
   328	    return (year_data.iloc[-1] / high) * 100
   329	
   330	
   331	def compute_returns(hist):
   332	    """Compute all return columns from a price history Series."""
   333	    if hist is None or (hasattr(hist, '__len__') and len(hist) == 0):
   334	        return {col: None for col in RETURN_COLS}
   335	    returns = {}
   336	    for year in ANNUAL_YEARS:
   337	        returns[str(year)] = calc_annual_return(hist, year)
   338	    returns["1D"] = calc_1d_return(hist)
   339	    returns["1W"] = calc_1w_return(hist)
   340	    returns["QTD"] = calc_qtd_return(hist)
   341	    returns["YTD"] = calc_ytd_return(hist)
   342	    returns["1Y"] = calc_period_return(hist, 365)
   343	    returns["3Y"] = calc_period_return(hist, 365 * 3)
   344	    returns["5Y"] = calc_period_return(hist, 365 * 5)
   345	    returns["10Y"] = calc_period_return(hist, 365 * 10)
   346	    returns["% 52Wk Hi"] = calc_pct_of_52wk_high(hist)
   347	    return returns
   348	
   349	
   350	def build_result_row(ticker, company, sector, subsector, yf_sector, yf_industry,
   351	                     country_iso, exchange, returns, fund, is_ttm, currency,
   352	                     core=""):
   353	    """Build a standardized result row dict."""
   354	    def _clean(val):
   355	        return val if val != "nan" else ""
   356	
   357	    row = {
   358	        "Ticker": ticker,
   359	        "Company Name": _clean(company),
   360	        "Sector (JP)": _clean(sector),
   361	        "Subsector (JP)": _clean(subsector),
   362	        "Core": _clean(core),
   363	        "YF Sector": _clean(yf_sector),
   364	        "YF Industry": _clean(yf_industry),
   365	        "Country (ISO)": _clean(country_iso),
   366	        "Exchange": _clean(exchange),
   367	        "_is_ttm_rev": is_ttm["Rev Grw"],
   368	        "_is_ttm_eps": is_ttm["EPS Grw"],
   369	        "_currency": currency,
   370	    }
     1	"""FMP TTM cash-return metrics — FCF yield, ROIC and CFO margin for the whole universe.
     2	
     3	Distinct from `fmp_provider.py`, which is the TTM/profile fundamentals chain, because that
     4	chain is `yf_first`: when yfinance answers with a market cap and the row looks complete, the
     5	FMP leg is never called at all. These three columns must exist for EVERY row or the screens
     6	downstream silently run over whoever yfinance happened to miss, so they get their own step —
     7	the same shape as `fmp_history.py`, which is here for the same reason.
     8	
     9	Endpoint: `/stable/key-metrics-ttm?symbol=X` — ONE call carries all three numbers.
    10	JP, 2026-09-22, asked for a mid-teens FCF-yield screen; board `#430` asks for negative
    11	FCF/CFO with ROIC above 15% and `#361` for ROIC quintiles. Fetching them separately would
    12	have made three callers of one endpoint on three cadences — three chances to disagree about
    13	one company on one day.
    14	
    15	⛑ EVERY STORED FIELD IS A RATIO, AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE. Measured 2026-09-22, FMP's
    16	`marketCap` and `investedCapitalTTM` are in the LISTING'S OWN CURRENCY for cross-listings:
    17	Takeda's is 150.3x Coverage Manager's USD figure (yen), Novo's 6.55x (kroner), GSK's 0.72x
    18	(sterling). An absolute field would be a local-currency number in a report whose money
    19	columns are all USD, and a "$10bn" gate over it is the pence trap this fleet has already
    20	paid for twice. A ratio has the same currency top and bottom, so it is unit-free and safe.
    21	`mcap_usd` in the perf report remains the only market cap anything may threshold on.
    22	
    23	CFO margin is DERIVED, not fetched: `evToSalesTTM / evToOperatingCashFlowTTM` is
    24	(EV/Sales)·(OCF/EV) = OCF/Sales. Validated against the quarterly cash-flow and income
    25	statements on 8 names, including three with negative operating cash flow (MRNA -47.2%,
    26	SRPT -4.6%, BEAM -230.3%): exact to the printed digits on 7, the 8th being the vendor's own
    27	disagreement documented below. That saves a second endpoint for the `#430` leg entirely.
    28	
    29	Status semantics — "no silent failures", the same four words `fmp_history` uses:
    30	  "ok"            → at least one of the three numbers came back usable
    31	  "no_data"       → FMP answered and had nothing for this ticker. A RECORDED FACT, cached on
    32	                    a shorter TTL, visibly different from "never tried". 225 of 1,359
    33	                    coverage rows are in this state and 80% of them are foreign lines.
    34	  "gated"         → HTTP 402: the endpoint is not on this plan. Not an error, not retried.
    35	  "error"         → the fetch raised or the API misbehaved. NEVER cached, so the next run
    36	                    retries it.
    37	  "not_attempted" → no cache entry and the caller ran cache-only. No call was made.
    38	
    39	⛑ THE VENDOR DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ON SOME NAMES, SO A HEADLINE NUMBER IS CORROBORATED
    40	BEFORE IT CAN DRIVE A SCREEN. Measured 2026-09-22 across 8 names: FMP's
    41	`freeCashFlowYieldTTM` equals its own four quarterly cash-flow statements over its own market
    42	cap to the printed digit on 7 of them — and on SANOFI it reads 18.45% against 13.18% from its
    43	statements, a 1.40x gap. SNY clears a 15% bar on the vendor's figure and fails it on the
    44	vendor's own filings. So every name that would PASS a mid-teens bar gets one extra call and a
    45	`Cash Flow Status` of `ok` or `unreconciled`; names nowhere near the bar are `not_checked`,
    46	which is cheap and honest rather than a blanket claim of verification.
    47	"""
    48	
    49	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
    50	
    51	from cache import cache_get, cache_set
    52	from logging_utils import get_logger, log_exception
    53	from providers.fmp_provider import _fmp_request, _safe_float, FMP_GATED_STATUS
    54	
    55	logger = get_logger("providers.fmp_quality")
    56	
    57	QUALITY_CACHE_NAMESPACE = "quality_metrics"
    58	# 6 days: the perf report is weekly, so this refreshes on every run rather than serving a
    59	# figure from the previous one. Market cap sits in the FCF-yield denominator and moves daily,
    60	# so a long TTL would quietly widen the as-of gap the report's own date claims.
    61	QUALITY_CACHE_TTL_HOURS = 144.0
    62	QUALITY_NO_DATA_TTL_HOURS = 168.0
    63	# ⛑ BUMPED TO 2 WHEN `stmt_as_of` LANDED. A v1 entry was corroborated but carries NO
    64	# statement date, and the consumer's staleness gate passes anything it cannot date — so 130
    65	# cached rows would have published as corroborated-and-undatable, which is exactly the
    66	# `a-check-that-silently-matches-nothing` shape (Codex r13). An old-schema entry is a cache
    67	# MISS and is refetched, the same rule `fmp_history` uses for its own v1 payloads.
    68	QUALITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2
    69	
    70	STATUS_OK = "ok"
    71	STATUS_NO_DATA = "no_data"
    72	STATUS_ERROR = "error"
    73	STATUS_GATED = "gated"
    74	STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED = "not_attempted"
    75	
    76	CHECK_OK = "ok"
    77	CHECK_UNRECONCILED = "unreconciled"
    78	CHECK_NO_STATEMENTS = "no_statements"
    79	CHECK_NOT_CHECKED = "not_checked"
    80	
    81	# A name at or above this on either leg is a screen candidate and gets corroborated.
    82	# It is deliberately BELOW the screens' own 15% bar: a name at 14.6% that the vendor has
    83	# overstated would otherwise reach the bar next week with no check ever having run.
    84	CHECK_TRIGGER = 0.12
    85	# How far the vendor's own statements may sit from its headline before the row is flagged.
    86	# SNY's live gap is 40%; the seven names that agree sit under 1%.
    87	CHECK_TOLERANCE = 0.20
    88	
    89	
    90	def _empty(status):
    91	    return {
    92	        "schema": QUALITY_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    93	        "status": status,
    94	        "fcf_yield": None,
    95	        "roic": None,
    96	        "cfo_margin": None,
    97	        "ic_nonpositive": False,
    98	        "check": CHECK_NOT_CHECKED,
    99	        "own_fcf_yield": None,
   100	        # The newest quarterly statement behind the corroboration, so a consumer can refuse
   101	        # a figure computed off an obsolete fiscal period. Only populated where we actually
   102	        # read statements: `key-metrics-ttm` carries NO period date at all (probed live
   103	        # 2026-09-22 -- 43 fields, not one of them a date), so for a row we never
   104	        # corroborated there is nothing honest to publish here.
   105	        "stmt_as_of": None,
   106	    }
   107	
   108	
   109	def _is_error_payload(data):
   110	    return isinstance(data, dict) and any(
   111	        k in data for k in ("Error Message", "error", "message"))
   112	
   113	
   114	def _fetch_key_metrics_ttm(ticker, api_key):
   115	    """(row, errored, gated) for /stable/key-metrics-ttm."""
   116	    try:
   117	        url = (f"https://financialmodelingprep.com/stable/key-metrics-ttm"
   118	               f"?symbol={ticker}&apikey={api_key}")
   119	        data, code = _fmp_request(url, want_status=True)
   120	        if data is None and code == FMP_GATED_STATUS:
   121	            return {}, False, True
   122	        if data is None:
   123	            logger.warning("FMP key-metrics-ttm gave no payload for %s (HTTP %s) — retryable "
   124	                           "error, not 'no data'", ticker, code)
   125	            return {}, True, False
   126	        if _is_error_payload(data):
   127	            return {}, True, False
   128	        if isinstance(data, list):
   129	            return (data[0] if data else {}), False, False
   130	        if isinstance(data, dict):
   131	            return data, False, False
   132	        return {}, True, False
   133	    except Exception as e:
   134	        log_exception(logger, f"FMP key-metrics-ttm failed for {ticker}", e)
   135	        return {}, True, False
   136	
   137	
   138	def _fetch_quarterly_fcf(ticker, api_key, limit=4):
   139	    """(sum of the last `limit` quarterly free cash flows, newest statement date, errored).
   140	
   141	    The sum is in the STATEMENT's currency, which is the same currency as the `marketCap`
   142	    in the key-metrics payload it is compared against — measured on SNY, both EUR. The
   143	    comparison is therefore currency-safe without touching an FX table.
   144	    """
   145	    try:
   146	        url = (f"https://financialmodelingprep.com/stable/cash-flow-statement"
   147	               f"?symbol={ticker}&period=quarter&limit={limit}&apikey={api_key}")
   148	        data, code = _fmp_request(url, want_status=True)
   149	        if not isinstance(data, list) or not data:
   150	            return None, None, (data is None and code != FMP_GATED_STATUS)
   151	        vals = [_safe_float(r.get("freeCashFlow")) for r in data]
   152	        if any(v is None for v in vals) or len(vals) < limit:
   153	            # A partial year is not a TTM. Corroborating against one would manufacture a
   154	            # disagreement out of the missing quarters.
   155	            return None, None, False
   156	        dates = sorted(str(r.get("date") or "")[:10] for r in data)
   157	        return sum(vals), (dates[-1] or None), False
   158	    except Exception as e:
   159	        log_exception(logger, f"FMP quarterly cash-flow failed for {ticker}", e)
   160	        return None, None, True
   161	
   162	
   163	def _corroborate(ticker, api_key, payload, market_cap):
   164	    """Set `check`/`own_fcf_yield` on a candidate row. Mutates and returns `payload`."""
   165	    own_fcf, stmt_as_of, errored = _fetch_quarterly_fcf(ticker, api_key)
   166	    payload["stmt_as_of"] = stmt_as_of
   167	    if own_fcf is None or not market_cap:
   168	        payload["check"] = CHECK_NO_STATEMENTS if not errored else CHECK_NOT_CHECKED
   169	        return payload
   170	    own_yield = own_fcf / market_cap
   171	    payload["own_fcf_yield"] = own_yield
   172	    vendor = payload.get("fcf_yield")
   173	    if vendor is None or vendor == 0:
   174	        payload["check"] = CHECK_NO_STATEMENTS
   175	        return payload
   176	    # A RATIO, not a difference in points: the same 2-point gap means something different at
   177	    # 3% and at 30%, and this bar has to hold across a universe spanning both.
   178	    payload["check"] = (CHECK_OK if abs(own_yield / vendor - 1.0) <= CHECK_TOLERANCE
   179	                        else CHECK_UNRECONCILED)
   180	    if payload["check"] == CHECK_UNRECONCILED:
   181	        logger.warning("%s: FMP headline FCF yield %.1f%% vs %.1f%% from its own quarterly "
   182	                       "statements — flagged unreconciled", ticker,
   183	                       vendor * 100, own_yield * 100)
   184	    return payload
   185	
   186	
   187	def fetch_quality(ticker, api_key, use_cache=True, cache_only=False):
   188	    """TTM FCF yield, ROIC and CFO margin for one ticker. Never raises."""
   189	    key = ticker.upper()
   190	    if use_cache:
   191	        cached = cache_get(QUALITY_CACHE_NAMESPACE, key, QUALITY_CACHE_TTL_HOURS)
   192	        if isinstance(cached, dict) and cached.get("schema") == QUALITY_SCHEMA_VERSION:
   193	            return cached
   194	    if cache_only or not api_key:
   195	        return _empty(STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED)
   196	
   197	    row, errored, gated = _fetch_key_metrics_ttm(ticker, api_key)
   198	    if gated:
   199	        out = _empty(STATUS_GATED)
   200	        cache_set(QUALITY_CACHE_NAMESPACE, key, out)
   201	        return out
   202	    if errored:
   203	        return _empty(STATUS_ERROR)          # never cached — retry next run
   204	    if not row:
   205	        out = _empty(STATUS_NO_DATA)
   206	        cache_set(QUALITY_CACHE_NAMESPACE, key, out)
   207	        return out
   208	
   209	    out = _empty(STATUS_NO_DATA)
   210	    fcf_yield = _safe_float(row.get("freeCashFlowYieldTTM"))
   211	    # ⛑ An exact 0.0 is FMP's "no data", not a company whose free cash flow is precisely
   212	    # zero. `sp500_valuation` learned this on `epsAvg == 0` for a profitable insurer; 12
   213	    # names in the fleet's existing FCF cache sit at exactly 0.0.
   214	    out["fcf_yield"] = None if fcf_yield == 0 else fcf_yield
   215	
   216	    roic = _safe_float(row.get("returnOnInvestedCapitalTTM"))
   217	    invested = _safe_float(row.get("investedCapitalTTM"))
   218	    if invested is not None and invested <= 0:
   219	        # ⛑ A return on NEGATIVE invested capital is not a high return — the sign of the
   220	        # denominator flips a loss into a flattering percentage. The guard lives HERE, at the
   221	        # one place the number is made, so no consumer can reach the unguarded value.
   222	        out["ic_nonpositive"] = True
   223	        out["roic"] = None
   224	    else:
   225	        out["roic"] = roic
   226	
   227	    ev_ocf = _safe_float(row.get("evToOperatingCashFlowTTM"))
   228	    ev_sales = _safe_float(row.get("evToSalesTTM"))
   229	    if ev_ocf not in (None, 0) and ev_sales is not None:
   230	        out["cfo_margin"] = ev_sales / ev_ocf
   231	
   232	    if any(out[f] is not None for f in ("fcf_yield", "roic", "cfo_margin")):
   233	        out["status"] = STATUS_OK
   234	
   235	    market_cap = _safe_float(row.get("marketCap"))
   236	    candidate = ((out["fcf_yield"] is not None and abs(out["fcf_yield"]) >= CHECK_TRIGGER)
   237	                 or (out["roic"] is not None and out["roic"] >= CHECK_TRIGGER))
   238	    if candidate:
   239	        out = _corroborate(ticker, api_key, out, market_cap)
   240	
   241	    cache_set(QUALITY_CACHE_NAMESPACE, key, out)
   242	    return out
   243	
   244	
   245	def fetch_quality_parallel(tickers, api_key, max_workers=10, use_cache=True,
   246	                           cache_only=False, progress_every=50):
   247	    """{ticker: payload} for many tickers. A failure is recorded, never raised."""
   248	    out = {}
   249	    if not tickers:
   250	        return out
   251	
   252	    def _one(t):
   253	        return t, fetch_quality(t, api_key, use_cache=use_cache, cache_only=cache_only)
   254	
   255	    completed, total = 0, len(tickers)
   256	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   257	        futures = {executor.submit(_one, t): t for t in tickers}
   258	        for future in as_completed(futures):
   259	            try:
   260	                t, payload = future.result()
   261	                out[t] = payload
   262	            except Exception as e:
   263	                t = futures[future]
   264	                log_exception(logger, f"FMP quality failed for {t}", e)
   265	                out[t] = _empty(STATUS_ERROR)
   266	            completed += 1
   267	            if progress_every and completed % progress_every == 0:
   268	                logger.info("FMP quality %s/%s...", completed, total)
   269	    return out
   270	
   271	
   272	def quality_columns_from_payload(payload):
   273	    """Payload → the report's column dict. Percentages, because every neighbouring
   274	    percentage column in this report (`ROE (TTM)`, `Gross Mgn (TTM)`) is one."""
   275	    p = payload or _empty(STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED)
   276	
   277	    def _pct(v):
   278	        return None if v is None else v * 100.0
   279	
   280	    return {
   281	        "FCF Yield": _pct(p.get("fcf_yield")),
   282	        "ROIC": _pct(p.get("roic")),
   283	        "CFO Margin": _pct(p.get("cfo_margin")),
   284	        "Cash Flow Status": _status_cell(p),
   285	        "Cash Flow As Of": p.get("stmt_as_of"),
   286	    }
   287	
   288	
   289	def _status_cell(p):
   290	    """One cell a reader can act on: why a number is missing, or why it is suspect.
   291	
   292	    `ok` alone would be ambiguous between "checked and agreed" and "fetched fine, never
   293	    checked", which is the distinction the corroboration exists to draw.
   294	    """
   295	    status = p.get("status", STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED)
   296	    if status != STATUS_OK:
   297	        return status
   298	    if p.get("check") == CHECK_UNRECONCILED:
   299	        return CHECK_UNRECONCILED
   300	    if p.get("check") == CHECK_OK:
   301	        return "ok (corroborated)"
   302	    # ⛑ "WE COULD NOT CHECK" IS NOT "WE CHECKED". A candidate whose statements were
   303	    # unavailable, or whose corroboration call failed, used to collapse into a plain `ok`
   304	    # cell — and screens_equity's mid-teens screen rejects only `unreconciled`, so an
   305	    # unverified figure published under a section promising corroboration (Codex r7).
   306	    fcf = p.get("fcf_yield")
   307	    candidate = fcf is not None and abs(fcf) >= CHECK_TRIGGER
   308	    if candidate and p.get("check") == CHECK_NO_STATEMENTS:
   309	        return "ok (not corroborated: no statements)"
   310	    if candidate and p.get("check") == CHECK_NOT_CHECKED:
   311	        return "ok (not corroborated)"
   312	    if p.get("ic_nonpositive"):
   313	        return "ok (ROIC withheld: invested capital <= 0)"
   314	    return STATUS_OK
     1	"""Valuation arithmetic shared by every lane that reads a vendor payload.
     2	
     3	⛑ THIS MODULE EXISTS BECAUSE THE RULE LIVED BESIDE ONE CONSUMER. `MINOR_UNITS`
     4	was defined in `scripts/build_hc_coverage_xlsx.py`, so when the coverage books
     5	were fixed on 2026-09-07 the weekly performance report -- a different lane
     6	reading the same vendor -- kept publishing Aspen Pharmacare 100x low for another
     7	day. `derive_valuation` was about to repeat that exactly: written for the
     8	workbook, with `reporting/generate.py` still deriving `Net Debt = EV - marketCap`
     9	on mixed units beside it. A rule that describes a VENDOR belongs beside the
    10	vendor, not beside one of its consumers.
    11	
    12	So this is the one implementation. `scripts/build_hc_coverage_xlsx.py` and
    13	`reporting/generate.py` both import from here; neither owns a copy.
    14	
    15	THE DEFECT IT ENCODES. Yahoo's `enterpriseValue` is `marketCap` (in the QUOTE
    16	currency) plus `totalDebt - totalCash` (in the REPORTING currency), summed as if
    17	they shared a unit. Measured 2026-09-08: `(EV - marketCap) / (totalDebt -
    18	totalCash)` is 1.000 TAK, 1.004 NVO, 0.990 LLY, 1.053 CYH. For a US row the two
    19	currencies match and the sum is harmless; for an ADR it is a number in no unit
    20	at all, and Takeda published at USD 5.1 trillion.
    21	"""
    22	import math
    23	
    24	from providers.fx_provider import MINOR_UNITS, major_unit  # noqa: F401  (re-export)
    25	
    26	
    27	def num(x):
    28	    """Vendor value -> float, or None for anything that is not a real number.
    29	
    30	    ⛑ REJECTS INFINITY, NOT JUST NaN (Codex, High, 2026-09-08). This was
    31	    `None if f != f else f`, which is a NaN test only, so +/-inf passed straight
    32	    through. That mattered because `size_bucket()` is derived from the raw value
    33	    BEFORE any downstream scrub: `marketCap=inf` published a BLANK market-cap
    34	    cell next to `Size = LC`, and -- worse -- it never counted toward the
    35	    partial-book guard's >5% missing-cap threshold, because the guard tests the
    36	    converted cell rather than the input.
    37	
    38	    Validating at the boundary is the fix: reject the value where it enters, so
    39	    Size, the ratios, the sort keys and the summary totals all inherit one
    40	    decision instead of each re-deriving from a contaminated input.
    41	    """
    42	    try:
    43	        f = float(x)
    44	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    45	        return None
    46	    return f if math.isfinite(f) else None
    47	
    48	
    49	def positive_multiple(raw):
    50	    """A valuation multiple, or None if it is not positive.
    51	
    52	    Same rule as `forward_pe` and for the same reason: a negative EV/EBITDA is a
    53	    loss-making denominator showing through the ratio, not a cheap company, and it
    54	    sorts straight to the top of any "cheapest names" ranking.
    55	    """
    56	    v = num(raw)
    57	    return v if (v is not None and v > 0) else None
    58	
    59	
    60	def _usable_rate(rate):
    61	    """A rate you can actually convert with: a positive, finite number.
    62	
    63	    Present-but-garbage is the case that bites. `fx.get(...) is not None` is true
    64	    for 0.0, for a negative, and for NaN, and each one produces a different
    65	    wrong answer rather than a blank.
    66	    """
    67	    if rate is None:
    68	        return False
    69	    try:
    70	        r = float(rate)
    71	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    72	        return False
    73	    return math.isfinite(r) and r > 0
    74	
    75	
    76	def derive_valuation(payload, fx):
    77	    """`{ev_usd_m, ev_sales, ev_ebitda, reporting_ccy, reason}` for one row.
    78	
    79	    ⛑ THE VENDOR'S `enterpriseValue` IS NOT IN ANY CURRENCY, so it is never
    80	    published. Measured 2026-09-08 across the live payloads: Yahoo's EV is
    81	    `marketCap` (in the QUOTE currency) plus `totalDebt - totalCash` (in the
    82	    REPORTING currency), summed as if they shared a unit --
    83	    `(EV - marketCap) / (totalDebt - totalCash)` is 1.000 for TAK, 1.004 for NVO,
    84	    0.990 for LLY, 1.053 for CYH. For a US row the two currencies are the same and
    85	    the sum is harmless; for an ADR it is a number in no unit at all.
    86	
    87	    ⛑ THAT IS WHY TAGGING EV WITH `financialCurrency` AND CONVERTING IS WRONG,
    88	    and it was the first fix proposed. It produces Takeda at USD 33.3bn against a
    89	    true ~USD 91.8bn: a PLAUSIBLE wrong number, which is worse than the absurd
    90	    USD 5.1tn it replaces, because absurd numbers get noticed and plausible ones
    91	    get used.
    92	
    93	    So: trust only primitives that each carry ONE known currency, and compute.
    94	
    95	        EV      = marketCap x fx(quote)  +  (totalDebt - totalCash) x fx(reporting)
    96	        EV/S    = EV / (totalRevenue x fx(reporting))
    97	        EV/EBITDA = EV / (ebitda x fx(reporting))
    98	
    99	    This also repairs a class that has nothing to do with currency: ASML and
   100	    argenx have entirely sane components and only the vendor's DERIVED EV is
   101	    broken (argenx quote and reporting are both USD and its EV was still 25x its
   102	    market cap). Computed: TAK EV 5,134,819 -> 91,798; NVO EV/S 0.9 -> 4.3;
   103	    ASML 1035.7 -> 15.9; ARGX 302.9 -> 11.1; CYH unchanged at 0.9, correctly.
   104	
   105	    ⛑ NO FALLBACK TO THE VENDOR EV WHEN A COMPONENT IS MISSING. That would
   106	    reintroduce exactly the undetectable garbage class, and it cannot be screened
   107	    out afterwards: Novo's published EV is 37% high while sitting INSIDE any
   108	    sane EV/market-cap band, and CYH is correct while sitting outside it. A ratio
   109	    test flags the innocent and passes the guilty, so the only honest gate is
   110	    "are this field's own inputs present and convertible" -- `reason` says which
   111	    one was not.
   112	
   113	    Known limit, stated because the number should not imply more precision than
   114	    it has: component EV omits minority interest and preferred stock, so it reads
   115	    ~0.5% below Yahoo's own primary-listing EV for TAK and ~2% for NVO. That is
   116	    far inside the error of any spot-FX conversion.
   117	    """
   118	    out = {"ev_usd_m": None, "ev_sales": None, "ev_ebitda": None,
   119	           "net_debt_usd": None, "revenue_usd_m": None,
   120	           "reporting_ccy": None, "reason": None}
   121	
   122	    quote = (payload.get("currency") or "").strip()
   123	    report = (payload.get("financialCurrency") or "").strip()
   124	    out["reporting_ccy"] = report or None
   125	
   126	    mc = num(payload.get("marketCap"))
   127	    debt = num(payload.get("totalDebt"))
   128	    cash = num(payload.get("totalCash"))
   129	
   130	    # ── REVENUE IS GATED ON ITS OWN INPUTS, BEFORE ANY EV GATE ────────────────
   131	    # ⛑ Codex Medium #6, 2026-09-08. Revenue needs exactly three things: the
   132	    # figure, the reporting currency, and a usable rate for it. It does NOT need
   133	    # a market cap, a quote currency, debt or cash -- yet every one of those
   134	    # early-returned above it, and `reporting/generate.py` blanks `Revenue (TTM)`
   135	    # whenever `ev_usd_m` is None. Trigger: `totalRevenue = 5e9`, reporting USD,
   136	    # `marketCap = None` -> the commercial-biopharma classifier correctly sees
   137	    # $5bn while the performance report published Revenue TTM as blank.
   138	    #
   139	    # This is the function's own stated rule finally applied to this field: "are
   140	    # THIS field's own inputs present and convertible". `_revenue_usd_m` in
   141	    # `universe/commercial_biopharma.py` exists solely because revenue could not
   142	    # be trusted to come out of here; the two now agree by construction.
   143	    #
   144	    # Zero stays a real, publishable answer (a pre-revenue biotech); a negative
   145	    # is not a revenue figure and stays absent.
   146	    _rev = num(payload.get("totalRevenue"))
   147	    if report and _rev is not None and _rev >= 0:
   148	        _r_rate_only = fx.get(major_unit(report))
   149	        if _usable_rate(_r_rate_only):
   150	            _rev_usd_m = _rev * _r_rate_only / 1e6
   151	            if math.isfinite(_rev_usd_m):
   152	                out["revenue_usd_m"] = _rev_usd_m
   153	
   154	    if mc is None or mc <= 0:
   155	        # ⛑ `mc == 0` is NOT a small company, it is a vendor blank wearing a
   156	        # number (Codex, 2026-09-08). It sails past an `is None` check and makes
   157	        # EV collapse to net debt alone: Takeda came out at USD 33,003M -- which
   158	        # is, to the dollar, the same plausible-wrong figure the rejected
   159	        # financialCurrency fix produced. A wrong EV that looks reasonable is the
   160	        # one failure mode this whole function exists to prevent.
   161	        out["reason"] = "no marketCap"; return out
   162	    if not quote:
   163	        out["reason"] = "no quote currency"; return out
   164	    if not report:
   165	        # Absent for some rows in `.info`. That is a blank, never a fallback to
   166	        # the quote currency -- assuming they match is the original defect.
   167	        out["reason"] = "no financialCurrency"; return out
   168	    if debt is None or cash is None:
   169	        out["reason"] = "no totalDebt/totalCash"; return out
   170	
   171	    # ⛑ A RATE MUST BE POSITIVE AND FINITE, not merely present (Codex,
   172	    # 2026-09-08). `fetch_aggregate_fx` can hand back 0.0 or a negative for a
   173	    # dead pair, and all three of those failed differently and badly:
   174	    #   0.0 on the reporting leg -> ZeroDivisionError in the EV/Sales
   175	    #     denominator. A CRASH, and it beat the `dead_fx` guard to the punch --
   176	    #     that guard runs AFTER this loop, so it could never report the thing it
   177	    #     exists to report. Ordering made a guard unreachable.
   178	    #   negative on the reporting leg -> a confident USD 25,470M for Takeda with
   179	    #     `reason: None`, i.e. published as though proven.
   180	    #   0.0 on the quote leg -> a near-zero EV, also with no reason.
   181	    # `is None` was the wrong test. "Can I actually convert with this?" is the
   182	    # right one, and it is asked of both legs before either is used.
   183	    q_rate = fx.get(major_unit(quote))
   184	    r_rate = fx.get(major_unit(report))
   185	    if not _usable_rate(q_rate):
   186	        out["reason"] = "no FX for %s" % quote; return out
   187	    if not _usable_rate(r_rate):
   188	        out["reason"] = "no FX for %s" % report; return out
   189	
   190	    # ⛑ `net_debt_usd` IS RETURNED, NOT RECOMPUTED BY THE CALLER (Fable, Low #4,
   191	    # 2026-09-08). `reporting/generate.py` used to re-derive this leg from the raw
   192	    # payload -- a SECOND implementation of a value this function had already
   193	    # proven, and it skipped `num()`, so a vendor string `"5.4e12"` passed the
   194	    # checks here and then raised TypeError on `debt - cash` in the caller,
   195	    # aborting the whole report. One computation, one place.
   196	    net_debt_usd = (debt - cash) * r_rate
   197	    ev_usd = mc * q_rate + net_debt_usd
   198	    if not math.isfinite(ev_usd):
   199	        out["reason"] = "non-finite EV"; return out
   200	    out["ev_usd_m"] = ev_usd / 1e6
   201	    out["net_debt_usd"] = net_debt_usd if math.isfinite(net_debt_usd) else None
   202	
   203	    # Belt and braces on the denominator itself. `r_rate` is positive and both
   204	    # figures are checked positive above, so the product should be too -- but a
   205	    # tiny revenue times a tiny rate can underflow to exactly 0.0, and this is a
   206	    # division. Guarding the RESULT (as positive_multiple does) is too late; the
   207	    # exception is raised before it ever sees a value.
   208	    # ⛑ REVENUE IS RETURNED, NOT LEFT AS AN INTERMEDIATE. It is already computed
   209	    # here (`totalRevenue x fx(reporting)`) and it is the input to the commercial
   210	    # -biopharma classification and to the revenue-vs-market-cap screen. The
   211	    # alternative every consumer reached for first was deriving it as
   212	    # `EV / (EV/Sales)`, which inherits any error in EITHER input and returns
   213	    # nothing for the rows with no EV/Sales at all.
   214	    #
   215	    # Note ZERO is a real, publishable answer -- a pre-revenue biotech -- and is
   216	    # kept distinct from None. `ev_sales` still requires a POSITIVE denominator,
   217	    # so a zero-revenue row reports revenue 0.0 and no multiple.
   218	    # `revenue_usd_m` was already set above, on its own inputs alone. Only the
   219	    # MULTIPLE is computed here, because that one genuinely needs the EV.
   220	    rev = num(payload.get("totalRevenue"))

   455	def _fmt_duration(seconds):
   456	    """Format seconds as human-readable duration."""
   457	    if seconds < 60:
   458	        return f"{seconds:.1f}s"
   459	    m, s = divmod(int(seconds), 60)
   460	    if m < 60:
   461	        return f"{m}m {s}s"
   462	    h, m = divmod(m, 60)
   463	    return f"{h}h {m}m {s}s"

     8	def run_step(name, fn, *args, **kwargs):
     9	    """Run a pipeline step, catching and logging failures.
    10	
    11	    Returns (status_string, result_or_none). On success, status is "ok".
    12	    On failure, status is "failed: <exception message>".

    15	        result = fn(*args, **kwargs)

    28	        decision (e.g. validation failed and --force was not passed)
    29	
    30	    Both are operationally non-success: a blocked report run produced no
    31	    report, just like a failed run did. Distinguishing them is for debugging
    32	    only and the prefix is preserved in the status string.
    33	
    34	    Statuses like "ok", "skipped", "skipped (dry run)", and "skipped: <reason>"

    36	    choices.

    38	    return [

    41	        if isinstance(v, str) and (v.startswith("failed") or v.startswith("blocked"))
    42	    ]

   133	def _ascii(text: str) -> str:
   134	    """Escape anything a cp1252 console cannot print.
   135	
   136	    Sanitize the DATA, not just the format string: this universe is global
   137	    (`R0DE`, `Tickér`, Japanese and Nordic company names all reach these
   138	    messages through fieldnames, tickers and OS error text), and a
   139	    UnicodeEncodeError would kill the run at the exact moment it is trying to
   140	    report why the publish is broken.
   141	    """
   142	    return text.encode("ascii", "backslashreplace").decode("ascii")

   145	def _dedupe(problems: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   146	    """Drop exact repeats, preserving order.
   147	
   148	    universe_status.json is the status file for BOTH universe.csv and
   149	    universe_metadata.json, so one corrupt status file is discovered twice.
   150	    Identical strings carry identical information; reporting them twice only
   151	    makes the operator wonder what the difference is.
   152	    """
   153	    seen: set[str] = set()
   154	    out: list[str] = []
   155	    for p in problems:
   156	        if p not in seen:
   157	            seen.add(p)
   158	            out.append(p)
   159	    return out

   162	def _read_csv_strict(p: Path, problems: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]] | None:
   163	    """Open a published CSV exactly as the least-tolerant consumer does.
   164	
   165	    Returns (fieldnames, rows), or None after recording the problem. An
   166	    unreadable file is a FINDING, not a crash — the acceptance step must report
   167	    WHICH artifact is broken, not die on the first bad byte.
   168	    """
   169	    # Sniff three bytes, not the whole file: universe.csv is multi-MB and
   170	    # `read_bytes()[:3]` loaded all of it to look at the header.
   171	    try:
   172	        with p.open("rb") as fh:
   173	            head = fh.read(3)
   174	    except OSError as e:
   175	        # `exists()` is true for a locked file, a permission-denied file and a
   176	        # directory alike; only the open tells them apart. exports/ lives in
   177	        # Dropbox, which briefly locks files mid-sync, so this is the likeliest
   178	        # way the weekly pipeline meets an unreadable artifact.
   179	        problems.append(
   180	            f"{p.name}: could not be opened ({type(e).__name__}: {e}) - the "
   181	            f"artifact exists but was NOT checked, so nothing here says whether "
   182	            f"it is publishable")
   183	        return None
   184	    if head == _BOM:
   185	        problems.append(
   186	            f"{p.name}: starts with a UTF-8 BOM. A consumer reading plain utf-8 sees "
   187	            f"'\\ufeff...' as its first header cell and silently recovers nothing.")
   188	
   189	    try:
   190	        with p.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
   191	            reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
   192	            fields = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
   193	            rows = list(reader)
   194	    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
   195	        problems.append(
   196	            f"{p.name}: not valid UTF-8 (byte {e.object[e.start:e.start + 1]!r} at "
   197	            f"offset {e.start}) - a plain-utf-8 consumer crashes on this file")
   198	        return None
   199	    except csv.Error as e:
   200	        # A single cell over csv's 131,072-char field limit (one bloated Notes
   201	        # value) aborts `list(reader)`. Every consumer using stock csv hits the
   202	        # same wall, so this is a publish defect, not a checker limitation -
   203	        # raising our own field limit would only hide it.
   204	        problems.append(
   205	            f"{p.name}: unreadable as CSV ({e}) - a consumer using stock csv "
   206	            f"fails on this file the same way")
   207	        return None
   208	    except OSError as e:
   209	        problems.append(
   210	            f"{p.name}: could not be read ({type(e).__name__}: {e}) - the "
   211	            f"artifact was NOT checked")
   212	        return None

   253	def _read_status(sp: Path, problems: list[str]) -> dict | None:

   255	
   256	    `null` is what a truncated or failed atomic write leaves behind, and

   273	def _expected_count(sp: Path, count_field: str, problems: list[str]) -> int | None:

   275	
   276	    Every non-answer below used to be a silent skip: absent file, BOM, corrupt
   277	    JSON, wrong shape, missing field, non-numeric field. A status file that

   283	            f"read pattern STARTS by asserting on this file, and the row-count "
   284	            f"cross-check it exists for could not be made")

   286	    status = _read_status(sp, problems)
   287	    if status is None:

   289	    if count_field not in status:
   290	        problems.append(
   291	            f"{sp.name}: no '{count_field}' field - the row-count cross-check "
   292	            f"silently did not run")

   294	    value = status[count_field]
   295	    # `True` is an int in Python, so a boolean has to be rejected explicitly or
   296	    # it would compare against a row count as 1.

   299	            f"{sp.name}: '{count_field}' is {type(value).__name__} "
   300	            f"({value!r}), not a row count - the cross-check silently did not run")

   334	        problems.append(
   335	            f"ticker_aliases.json: expected a JSON object, got "
   336	            f"{type(payload).__name__} - no consumer can resolve a symbol from this")

   338	
   339	    amap = payload.get("alias_to_canonical")
   340	    entries = payload.get("entries")

   343	            "ticker_aliases.json: needs an 'alias_to_canonical' object and an "
   344	            "'entries' array - a consumer reading either one alone would silently "
   345	            "resolve nothing")
   346	        return problems

   351	    entry_vendors: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
   352	    for e in entries:

   144	def dedupe_sec_quarter_labels(units: dict) -> dict[str, list]:
   145	    """SEC companyconcept `units` → {period_end: [fy, quarter]} (Q1–Q3, original filing)."""
   146	    cand: dict[str, tuple[int, int, str]] = {}  # end -> (fy, q, filed)
   147	    for rows in units.values():
   148	        for r in rows:
   149	            fp, fy, end, start = r.get("fp"), r.get("fy"), r.get("end"), r.get("start")
   150	            form, filed = r.get("form"), r.get("filed")
   151	            if not (fp and fy and end and start and filed) or form not in ("10-Q", "10-Q/A"):
   152	                continue
   153	            q = {"Q1": 1, "Q2": 2, "Q3": 3}.get(fp)
   154	            if q is None:
   155	                continue
   156	            dur = (datetime.date.fromisoformat(end) - datetime.date.fromisoformat(start)).days
   157	            if not (80 <= dur <= 100):
   158	                continue
   159	            if end not in cand or filed < cand[end][2]:
   160	                cand[end] = (int(fy), q, filed)

   169	def anchor_count(report_dates: list[str], anchor: dict | None) -> dict[str, list]:
   170	    """{report_date: [fy, q]} by anchoring on Finnhub's explicit label and counting
   171	    over the ordered report-date list (immune to 4-4-5 / 52-53-week calendars)."""
   172	    if not anchor:
   173	        return {}
   174	    dates = sorted(set(report_dates) | {anchor["date"]})
   175	    if anchor["date"] not in dates:
   176	        return {}
   177	    ai = dates.index(anchor["date"])
   178	    out: dict[str, list] = {}
   179	    y, q = anchor["year"], anchor["quarter"]
   180	    prev = None
   181	    for i in range(ai, -1, -1):              # backward incl. anchor
   182	        d = datetime.date.fromisoformat(dates[i])
   183	        if prev is not None and (prev - d).days > GAP_BREAK_DAYS:
   184	            break                            # missing quarter → stop counting
   185	        out[dates[i]] = [y, q]
   186	        prev = d
   187	        y, q = _advance(y, q, -1)
   188	    y, q = _advance(anchor["year"], anchor["quarter"], 1)
   189	    prev = datetime.date.fromisoformat(anchor["date"])
   190	    for i in range(ai + 1, len(dates)):      # forward
   191	        d = datetime.date.fromisoformat(dates[i])
   192	        if (d - prev).days > GAP_BREAK_DAYS:
   193	            break
   194	        out[dates[i]] = [y, q]
   195	        prev = d
   196	        y, q = _advance(y, q, 1)
   197	    return out

   200	def _fye_month_from(period_end_iso: str, quarter: int) -> int:
   201	    """Infer the fiscal-year-end month from one labeled quarter. Snaps the
   202	    period-end to the nearest calendar quarter month (3/6/9/12) first so 52/53-week
   203	    calendars whose quarter-ends spill into the next month (e.g. KO Q1 → Apr-3)
   204	    don't shift the inferred FYE by a month."""
   205	    m = datetime.date.fromisoformat(period_end_iso).month
   206	    qmonth = min((3, 6, 9, 12), key=lambda c: min((m - c) % 12, (c - m) % 12))
   207	    return ((qmonth - 3 * quarter - 1) % 12) + 1

   272	    recent_disagree = len(recent_both) - recent_agree

   295	        "sources": sources_meta or {},

   297	        "recent_quarters": rows,

   303	def _is_monotonic(rows: list[dict]) -> bool:
   304	    keys = [r["fiscal_year"] * 4 + r["fiscal_quarter"] for r in rows]  # newest-first
   305	    return all(keys[i] > keys[i + 1] for i in range(len(keys) - 1))

   313	def build_reporting_calendar(tickers, *, today=None, cik_map=None,

   315	    """Build the full calendar dict for `tickers`. Returns (calendar, status_meta).
   316	
   317	    Per-ticker raw pulls are cached (30-day TTL) under cache/reporting_calendar/.
   318	    Network failures degrade per-ticker (row present, gating_eligible=false) — never
   319	    crash the weekly run.
   320	    """
   321	    today = today or datetime.date.today()

   323	    CACHE_DIR_RC.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   324	    calendar = {}
   325	    covered = gating_n = uncovered = errors = 0
   326	    last_finnhub = [0.0]

   328	    for tk in tickers:
   329	        tk = tk.upper()
   330	        cache = CACHE_DIR_RC / f"{tk}.json"
   331	        raw = None
   332	        if use_cache and cache.exists() and _age_days(cache) < CACHE_TTL_DAYS:
   333	            try:
   334	                raw = json.loads(cache.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   335	            except Exception:
   336	                raw = None
   337	        if raw is None:
   338	            cik = cik_map.get(tk)
   339	            sec_labels = fetch_sec_labels(cik) if cik else {}

   341	            if finnhub_spacing:
   342	                gap = time.monotonic() - last_finnhub[0]
   343	                if gap < finnhub_spacing:
   344	                    time.sleep(finnhub_spacing - gap)
   345	            finnhub_events = fetch_finnhub_events(tk, today)
   346	            last_finnhub[0] = time.monotonic()
   347	            ninjas_rows = fetch_ninjas_rows(tk)
   348	            raw = {

   350	                "sec_labels": sec_labels, "finnhub_events": finnhub_events,
   351	                "ninjas_rows": ninjas_rows,
   352	            }

   354	                cache.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")
   355	            except Exception as e:
   356	                logger.debug("cache write failed for %s: %s", tk, e)
   357	
   358	        sources_meta = {

   360	                      "n_rows": len(raw["ninjas_rows"]), "error": None},
   361	            "anchor": {"provider": "finnhub", "fetched_at": raw["fetched_at"],
   362	                       "n_events": len(raw["finnhub_events"]), "error": None},
   363	            "sec_label": {"provider": "sec_xbrl", "fetched_at": raw["fetched_at"],
   364	                          "covered": bool(raw["sec_labels"]), "error": None},
   365	        }
   366	        rec = build_record(
   367	            tk, sec_labels=raw["sec_labels"], finnhub_events=raw["finnhub_events"],
   368	            ninjas_rows=raw["ninjas_rows"], today=today, sources_meta=sources_meta,
   369	        )
   370	        calendar[tk] = rec

   373	        else:

   376	                (rec["next_expected"] or {}).get("gating_eligible"):

   379	    status = {

   382	        "non_us_or_uncovered_count": uncovered,
   383	        "gating_eligible_count": gating_n,
   384	        "generated_for": today.isoformat(),
   385	    }
   386	    return calendar, status

@echo off
setlocal
title CRSP Constituent Snapshot

REM ============================================================================
REM CRSP / Morningstar US Total Market constituent snapshot.
REM Run by the CrspQuarterlySnapshot task, Mondays at 08:00.
REM
REM WHY WEEKLY FOR A QUARTERLY FILE: CRSP OVERWRITES the constituents CSV each
REM quarter and keeps no archive, so a quarter missed is gone permanently. It
REM posts roughly a month after each rebalance, but the exact date drifts. A
REM weekly poll costs one 2 MB download and no-ops ("unchanged") whenever the
REM live TradeDate is already archived; a quarterly poll aimed at a drifting
REM date can silently miss one. The cheap run is the safe run.
REM
REM Unattended: NO `pause` (it hangs forever under Task Scheduler with no
REM console -> the task aborts as 0x8007042B). Full interpreter path per
REM CONVENTIONS.md. Surfaces python's exit code so a real failure shows red.
REM Exit 2 = download or verification failed; investigate, do not ignore.
REM CRLF + ASCII only.
REM ============================================================================

set "PYTHON_EXE=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Python314\python.exe"
cd /d "%USERPROFILE%\Dropbox\Claude Folder\Coverage Manager"

echo ============================================
echo   CRSP Constituent Snapshot
echo   %date% %time%
echo ============================================
echo.

REM Wrapped by run_guarded (board #287): this lane was measured BLIND -- it ran
REM every week and never heartbeated, so a failure stayed invisible until the
REM weekly monitor noticed, up to 7 days later. The wrapper posts an `error`
REM health/v1 heartbeat to #status-reports on a non-zero exit and re-exits with
REM the payload's own code, so a red task stays red. A healthy run is silent.
set "GUARD=%USERPROFILE%\Dropbox\Claude Folder\scheduled_jobs_monitor\run_guarded.py"
"%PYTHON_EXE%" "%GUARD%" --lane "CrspQuarterlySnapshot" --project "Coverage Manager" --cadence weekly -- "%PYTHON_EXE%" cli.py crsp-snapshot
set "RC=%errorlevel%"

echo.
echo ============================================
echo   Done (exit code %RC%).
echo ============================================
endlocal & exit /b %RC%

:fail
echo Coverage Manager enrich finished with errorlevel %RC%
endlocal & exit /b %RC%

   135	def write_html(df, path, today_str):
   136	    pct_cols = {"1D %", "1W %", "YTD %", "1Y %"}
   137	    price_cols = {"Current Price"}
   138	
   139	    header_html = "".join(f"<th>{c}</th>" for c in df.columns)
   140	    body_rows = []
   141	    for _, row in df.iterrows():
   142	        cells = []
   143	        for c in df.columns:
   144	            v = row[c]
   145	            if c in pct_cols:
   146	                txt = _fmt_num(v, pct=True)
   147	                color = ""
   148	                if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not pd.isna(v):
   149	                    if c == "% vs Target" and v < 0:
   150	                        color = "color:#1a7f37;"  # below target = green opportunity
   151	                    elif c == "% vs Buy" and v < 0:
   152	                        color = "color:#1a7f37;"  # below buy = green (can add)
   153	                    elif v > 0 and c in ("1D %", "1W %", "YTD %", "1Y %"):
   154	                        color = "color:#1a7f37;"
   155	                    elif v < 0 and c in ("1D %", "1W %", "YTD %", "1Y %"):
   156	                        color = "color:#b91c1c;"
   157	                cells.append(f"<td style='{color}text-align:right'>{txt}</td>")
   158	            elif c in price_cols:
   159	                cells.append(f"<td style='text-align:right'>{_fmt_num(v)}</td>")
   160	            else:
   161	                cells.append(f"<td>{'' if v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and pd.isna(v)) else v}</td>")
   162	        body_rows.append("<tr>" + "".join(cells) + "</tr>")
   163	
   164	    html = f"""<!doctype html>

   167	 body {{ font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif; margin: 24px; color: #111; }}
   168	 h1 {{ font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 6px; }}
   169	 .sub {{ color: #666; font-size: 12px; margin-bottom: 16px; }}
   170	 table {{ border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 12px; }}
   171	 th, td {{ border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 6px 10px; }}
   172	 th {{ background: #f5f5f5; text-align: left; }}
   173	 tr:nth-child(even) td {{ background: #fafafa; }}
   174	</style></head><body>
   175	<h1>Watchlist — {today_str}</h1>

   179	 <tbody>{''.join(body_rows)}</tbody>
   180	</table>
   181	</body></html>

   196	def format_slack_summary(df, today_str):

   203	        )

   207	def post_watchlist_to_slack(df, today_str, api_keys):
   208	    """Send the buy/target-gap summary to #portfolio. Returns True if it posted.
   209	
   210	    Moved off #stock-price-alerts 2026-08-10 (JP: "That table belongs in the portfolio
   211	    channel, not in price movements"). Two decisions worth keeping:
   212	
   213	    * **Bot token, not the webhook.** `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is permanently bound to
   214	      #stock-price-alerts, so this was never a channel-string edit.
   215	    * **No fallback to the old webhook.** If the bot path is unconfigured this skips
   216	      loudly. Falling back would keep posting to the exact channel he asked us to stop
   217	      posting to, and would look like success. The HTML + XLSX still go out by email,
   218	      so the cost of a skip is a convenience copy, not the report.
   219	
   220	    Never raises: the report has already been written and emailed by this point, and a
   221	    Slack outage must not turn a delivered report into a failed run.
   222	    """
   223	    token = api_keys.get("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN")
   224	    channel = api_keys.get("SLACK_PORTFOLIO_CHANNEL_ID")
   225	    if not (token and channel):
   226	        logger.warning(
   227	            "Slack: SKIPPED - need SLACK_BOT_TOKEN + SLACK_PORTFOLIO_CHANNEL_ID to "
   228	            "post to %s. Deliberately NOT falling back to the old "
   229	            "#stock-price-alerts webhook.", POSITIONS_CHANNEL)
   230	        return False
   231	    try:
   232	        post_to_channel(token, channel, format_slack_summary(df, today_str))
   233	        return True
   234	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - report already shipped by email
   235	        logger.warning("Slack: post to %s FAILED (%s). The HTML/XLSX email is "
   236	                       "unaffected.", POSITIONS_CHANNEL, e)
   237	        return False

   402	                f"auto-add row    : {len(self.auto_added)}"
   403	                f"  {', '.join(self.auto_added)}"
   404	                " - held at a broker, covered, no positions row existed"
   405	                " (board #347, JP 2026-09-26)"
   406	            )
   407	        if self.held_without_row:
   408	            # In the SUMMARY, not only in the CLI's warning block: `summary_lines` is
   409	            # what the dry run prints and what any other consumer of a plan reads, and
   410	            # a finding visible on only one of the two paths is half-reported.
   411	            out.append(
   412	                f"HELD, NO ROW    : {len(self.held_without_row)}"
   413	                f"  {', '.join(self.held_without_row)}"
   414	                " - owned, covered, and absent from the positions file; NOT auto-added "
   415	                f"(more than {MAX_AUTO_ADDS_PER_RUN} would be created in one run, or the "
   416	                "universe row lacks required metadata) (board #347)"
   417	            )
   418	        if self.withheld_demotions or self.withheld_refreshes:
   419	            out.append(
   420	                f"WITHHELD         : {len(self.withheld_demotions)} demotion(s)"
   421	                + (f" ({', '.join(self.withheld_demotions)})" if self.withheld_demotions else "")
   422	                + f", {len(self.withheld_refreshes)} figure update(s)"
   423	                + (f" ({', '.join(self.withheld_refreshes)})" if self.withheld_refreshes else "")
   424	                + " - the join could not be trusted this run"
   425	            )
   426	        if self.migrated_legacy:
   427	            out.append(
   428	                f"one-time migration of the retired 'Portfolio' Position value: "
   429	                f"{len(self.migrated_legacy)} row(s) -> {DEMOTION_POSITION}"
   430	            )
   431	        if self.already_sold:
   432	            out.append(
   433	                f"WAS Portfolio but absent from the broker feed -- recorded as "
   434	                f"previously held, sale date UNKNOWN (not inferred): "
   435	                f"{', '.join(self.already_sold)}"
   436	            )
   437	        if self.not_in_universe:
   438	            out.append(
   439	                f"HELD BUT NOT IN UNIVERSE: {', '.join(self.not_in_universe)} "
   440	                f"— NOT in Held: add it to the universe AND the positions file (or fix the "
   441	                f"symbol), then re-run sync-held"
   442	            )
   443	        return out
